summary: Design the architecture for a deep US political/electoral simulation game (Democracy-series inspired) across 6 subsystems, then synthesize a unified TS blueprint
logs: Got 6/6 subsystem designs. Synthesizing unified blueprint...

designs.overview:
This subsystem is the static-to-semi-static backbone the rest of the engine queries: it defines WHERE elections happen (jurisdictions), WHAT is being contested (offices/seats), HOW winners are chosen (electoral systems), and WHEN (the term/election schedule). It is almost entirely DATA, loaded from a JSON `ElectoralRuleset` bundle and validated at load. The engine layer (pure TS, no DOM) consumes it via a normalized, indexed in-memory store; the React UI is a pure projection over the same store plus derived selectors.

Design split. Three conceptual layers, all serializable:
(1) Definition layer (modder-authored, immutable at runtime): `Jurisdiction`, `OfficeDefinition`, `ElectoralSystemDef`, `TermRule`, `BallotMeasureType`, `Party`. These carry IDs and reference each other by ID only (no object nesting) so the whole graph is a flat normalized map keyed by string IDs — JSON-safe and diff-friendly for mods.
(2) Instance/seat layer (generated at new-game setup, then mutates with the sim): `Seat` (a single concrete winnable position, e.g. "US Senate, NY, Class 1"), `Officeholder` (who currently holds a seat), and the derived `ElectionSchedule` of upcoming `ElectionEvent`s. Seats are derived deterministically from definitions + jurisdiction data via a `materializeSeats(ruleset, seed)` pure function so saves can store just the ruleset id + seed + deltas, or the fully expanded set.
(3) Election-resolution layer: `ElectionInstance` (a specific contest on a specific date for one or more seats), `Candidacy`, and the `SeatAllocator` strategies (FPTP, two-round, RCV, multi-member/at-large block, party-list PR, Electoral College). Allocators are pure functions `(votesByCandidate, systemDef, rng) => AllocationResult` so they are trivially unit-testable and deterministic.

Why this shape. Democracy-4-style causal graphs and The-Political-Process-style granularity both need a stable, addressable set of "things you can win." By separating immutable definitions from mutable seats/holders, we get: deterministic regeneration from seed, cheap saves, clean modding (drop in a new state's JSON), and a single source of truth the campaign and governing subsystems both reference by `seatId`. The hierarchy is modeled as an adjacency tree (`parentId` + `JurisdictionKind` ordering) so containment queries (which districts are inside this county, which counties inside this state) are graph walks, not hardcoded. Every office ties to exactly one jurisdiction via `jurisdictionId`, and its winnable positions expand into N seats where N = `seatCount` (1 for single-member, M for at-large/multi-member, or computed from district children for district-based bodies like the US House).

Calendar coupling. The subsystem does not own the clock; it exposes `nextElectionsOnOrAfter(date)` and `seatsUpForElection(year, cycle)` given the global `GameCalendar`. Term staggering (Senate classes, half-of-council-every-2-years) is encoded in `TermRule.staggerGroup` + each seat's `classLabel`/`cohort`, so the scheduler is pure arithmetic over `firstElectionYear`, `termLengthYears`, and `cohort`.

mechanics: materializeSeats(ruleset, seed) → Seat[]: pure expansion. For each OfficeDefinition, resolve appliesToJurisdictionIds; for seatCount=1 emit one seat; for integer M emit M seats with cohorts assigned round-robin across TermRule.cohortCount; for 'per_district' emit one seat per child jurisdiction of matching kind; for 'apportioned' (US House) run apportionMethod first. Deterministic: cohort assignment uses a seeded shuffle so a state's Senate classes are stable per seed.

Apportionment (US House, 435): Huntington-Hill method of equal proportions. For each state give 1 seat, then iteratively assign seat n to the state with max priority = population / sqrt(n*(n+1)) until 435 assigned. Implemented as a priority queue; pure and testable against the real 2020 apportionment as a fixture.

Election scheduling: nextElectionYear(seat) = TermRule.firstElectionYearAnchor + cohortOffset + k*termLengthYears such that result >= currentYear, where cohortOffset = cohortIndex * (termLengthYears / cohortCount) for evenly staggered bodies (Senate: 6yr/3 classes → classes elected 2 years apart). electionDate resolved from electionDayRule (first_tuesday_after_first_monday_november = compute first Monday of Nov, add 1 day).

Term-limit check: eligibleToRun(person, seat) = TermRule.termLimit.type=='none' OR (type=='consecutive' AND person.consecutiveTermsInSeat < maxTerms) OR (type=='lifetime'/'absolute' AND person.termsServedTotal < maxTerms) OR (maxYears defined AND yearsServed+termLength <= maxYears). President: lifetime, 2 terms (with the >2yr-succession edge case: if served >2 years of another's term, max 1 elected term).
FPTP allocator: winner = argmax(votes). Ties → TermRule/system tieBreak (rng_seeded draws via seeded RNG; incumbent_wins). Returns margin = (top - second)/totalVotes.

Two-round/runoff: if topShare >= majorityThreshold → winner now; else schedule runoff ElectionInstance with runoffTopN candidates, parentElectionId set. Jungle/top-two: same but candidates from all parties advance regardless of party.

IRV/RCV allocator: iterative elimination. While no candidate has >50% of continuing ballots, eliminate lowest, redistribute to next-ranked continuing preference; exhausted ballots drop from denominator. Deterministic elimination tie-break via seeded RNG. Returns per-round tallies for UI replay.

STV multi-member: Droop quota = floor(validVotes/(seats+1))+1. Elect anyone over quota, transfer surplus by fractional transfer value = (surplus/candidateVotes); then eliminate lowest and transfer; repeat until seats filled. Gregory fractional method for determinism.
Block/at-large plurality: voter casts up to M votes; top M candidates win. Cumulative voting variant lets voters stack votes on fewer candidates.

Electoral College: resolve the presidential general as a meta-election over 51 state ElectionInstances. ecVotes(state) = houseSeats(state) + 2 (senators); DC = 3. winner_take_all: state's ECVs → state plurality winner. congressional_district (ME/NE): 2 ECVs to state plurality winner + 1 ECV per congressional-district plurality winner. Sum nationally; need >= 270 of 538. Tie/no-majority (269-269) → flag 'contingent_election' for the governing subsystem (House decides).

Vacancy handling: on holder death/resignation/removal, set seat.isVacant; consult OfficeDefinition.succession.vacancyMode → emit special ElectionInstance (triggeredBy='vacancy') OR appoint via appointerOfficeId OR promote running mate / next_in_line. TermRule.midTermVacancyTriggersSpecial gates whether a special is held vs appointment-until-next-general.

Recall: a recall petition validated against BallotMeasureType.qualification spawns an ElectionInstance(type='recall'); resolution either a yes/no question (then a separate replacement election) or a combined recall+replacement ballot, configurable per jurisdiction via electoralSystemId override.

Turnout model hook: turnout(election) = base[electionType] * jurisdiction modifiers; presidential general ~0.6 CVAP, midterm ~0.45, primary ~0.20, local off-cycle ~0.15. Actual votes = registeredVoters * turnout; this subsystem exposes the seated electorate, the demographics subsystem supplies the split. Stored on AllocationResult.turnout for audit.

Ballot-access gate: candidacy.qualifiesByFilingRules = signaturesCollected >= req.signatureCount && feePaid >= req.filingFeeUSD && age>=minAge && residencyYears>=req && citizenOk. Disqualified candidacies excluded from allocation but retained for history.

tddNotes: materializeSeats produces exactly 100 US Senate seats with cohorts distributed as 33/33/34 across class1/class2/class3 (2 per state, never same class twice in a state) and exactly 435 US House seats given 2020 census populations.
Huntington-Hill apportionment over the real 2020 state population fixture reproduces the official 2020 apportionment (CA=52, TX=38, FL=28, NY=26, ... MT=2, exactly 435 total, every state >=1).
Electoral College vote counts: sum over states+DC == 538; California==54, Texas==40, Wyoming==3, DC==3 (using 2020 apportionment + 2 + DC 3).

Senate class scheduling: given firstElectionYearAnchor and 6yr term, class1 next election years are 2024,2030,...; class2 2026; class3 2028 — nextElectionYear(seat) returns the correct staggered year for current date 2026-06-24.
electionDayRule first_tuesday_after_first_monday_november resolves to 2026-11-03 for year 2026 and 2024-11-05 for 2024.

FPTP allocator with votes {A:100,B:60,C:40} → winner A, margin == 40/200 == 0.2; a perfect tie {A:50,B:50} with tieBreak 'incumbent_wins' returns the incumbent and is deterministic across runs with same seed.

Two-round: {A:0.45,B:0.30,C:0.25}, majorityThreshold 0.5 → no winner, schedules runoff with candidates [A,B] (runoffTopN=2), parentElectionId set; with {A:0.55,...} → A wins outright, no runoff scheduled.
IRV: classic spoiler fixture where plurality leader loses after redistribution — verify final winner differs from first-round leader and exhausted ballots reduce the majority denominator correctly.
STV with Droop quota: 3 seats, validVotes=300 → quota = floor(300/4)+1 == 76; verify surplus transfer fractional values sum-preserving (no votes created/destroyed beyond exhaustion).

Term limits: a president having served 2 elected terms → eligibleToRun==false; one having served 2.5 years of a predecessor's term then 1 elected term → eligibleToRun==false (>2yr succession rule); a governor in a 'consecutive' 2-limit state who sat out a term → eligibleToRun==true.

Vacancy: killing a US Senator (midTermVacancyTriggersSpecial true, vacancyMode governor_appoints) marks seat vacant, creates an interim Officeholder via appointment AND schedules a special general at the next even-year November; a US House vacancy schedules an immediate special election (no appointment).

Maine/Nebraska EC: NE-style congressional_district mode splits a state's ECVs (2 statewide + 1 per CD); a fixture where state plurality is party X but one CD goes party Y yields Y winning exactly 1 ECV.

Jurisdiction containment: ancestorIds rebuilt on load such that a CD's ancestorIds == ['us','us-ny'] and isWithin('us-ny-cd-12','us-ny')==true, isWithin('us-ny-cd-12','us-ca')==false; overlapsJurisdictionIds handle a city spanning two counties without breaking the tree.

Serialization round-trip: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(store)) deep-equals the original ruleset+seats (no class instances, no Maps that lose key types, no Date objects — ISODate strings only), and a save storing only {rulesetId, seed, deltas} re-materializes identical seats.
Ballot-access gate: a candidacy below req.signatureCount has qualifiesByFilingRules==false and is excluded from AllocationResult yet retained in candidacyIds with filingStatus=='disqualified'.

Nonpartisan/unicameral edge: Nebraska legislature office has isPartisan==false, partisanLabelMode=='none', single chamber (no upper/lower split), and its seats carry no partyId requirement in candidacies.
risks: Real US data is enormous and inconsistent (≈520k elected offices, 50 different state constitutions). Mitigation: ship a small validated starter ruleset (federal + 2-3 example states fully, others as generated stubs) and make everything else moddable JSON; never hardcode state quirks in engine logic — push them into TermRule/ElectoralSystemDef data.

Per-state legal idiosyncrasies (jungle primaries in CA/WA/LA, RCV in ME/AK, retention elections, unicameral Nebraska, ticket vs separate Lt. Gov) can tempt special-case code. Mitigation: enforce that the engine reads only generic AllocationMethod/PrimaryStyle/TermRule fields; quirks must be expressible as data or the schema is extended, not branched.

Seat materialization determinism is load-bearing for saves; any nondeterminism (Object key order, unseeded shuffle, floating-point apportionment ties) corrupts save compatibility. Mitigation: seeded RNG everywhere, integer/rational math for apportionment priority where possible, golden-file tests on the expanded seat set.

Apportionment and redistricting change every 10 years and district geometry shifts; coupling seats tightly to fixed district ids breaks on re-census. Mitigation: model a 'cycle/vintage' on district jurisdictions and allow a re-apportionment event to regenerate House seats while preserving Senate/state seats.

Overlapping/non-tree jurisdictions (school districts crossing county lines, multi-county cities, special districts) don't fit a strict tree. Mitigation: keep the tree for containment but add overlapsJurisdictionIds and resolve electorates by explicit electorateId rather than inferring from the tree.

Scope creep into the demographics/voter and campaign subsystems. Mitigation: this subsystem stores only foreign keys (electorateId, personId, campaignId) and exposes the seat/electorate/schedule; turnout splits, candidate personas, and ad spend live elsewhere.

Electoral College contingent elections (no 270 majority, faithless electors, 269-269) are rare but real and easy to omit. Mitigation: AllocationResult carries a 'contingent_election' status the governing subsystem handles rather than silently picking a winner.

designs.overview:
This subsystem models a jurisdiction's electorate as a weighted set of overlapping demographic/values GROUPS (segments), never individual agents, for O(groups) performance with optional stochastic sampling only at the polling layer. It is a pure, deterministic TypeScript module living under `engine/electorate/` with no DOM/I/O. All state is a plain JSON-serializable object held in the master `GameState` under `gameState.jurisdictions[id].electorate`. The engine advances via discrete ticks (a `CampaignTick` ~= 1 day, an `OpinionTick` ~= 1 week aggregation) driven by the global calendar; UI reads computed selectors and never mutates.

Data-driven design: issues, demographic axes, group templates, and party definitions are loaded from JSON `data/*` registries keyed by stable string IDs. Engine logic operates only on those IDs + numeric params so the game is moddable. Positions are stored on a fixed [-1,1] continuous scale per issue (a multi-dimensional ideology vector), NOT left-right scalar.

The core pipeline each evaluation: for each (group g, candidate c) compute a deterministic UTILITY = weighted spatial proximity (salience-weighted squared/abs distance, negated) + valence/competence + favorability + name-recognition gating + partisan loyalty + incumbency/identity bonuses + noise-free systematic terms. Vote-share among groups is a softmax (multinomial logit) over candidate utilities scaled by a choice-sensitivity beta. TURNOUT is an independent per-group logistic of structural propensity + interest/mobilization + competitiveness. A group's contribution to a candidate = groupWeight * turnoutProb * voteShare. Summing over groups yields true latent support; POLLING draws a sampled, noisy, house-effect-biased, weighted estimate with a reported margin of error so the player never sees ground truth.

OPINION DYNAMICS evolve group state between ticks with inertia (exponential smoothing toward a target driven by economy, governing record, scandals, ad pressure, media tone, endorsements), so campaign actions and governing both move the same numbers. The module exposes: `evaluateElectorate(state, candidates, ctx)`, `runOpinionTick(state, events, rng)`, `conductPoll(state, pollSpec, rng)`, plus pure selectors for UI. Determinism is guaranteed by threading a single seeded splittable RNG (`mulberry32`/`splitmix64`) — RNG only enters opinion-event resolution and polling sampling; utility/turnout/share math is fully deterministic given state.

mechanics: EFFECTIVE IDEAL POINT (partisan pull): for group g, issue i, effIdeal = lerp(g.positions[i], party.platform[i], g.partisanStrength * party.baseLoyaltyPull). This bends a partisan's policy ideal toward their party's platform before distance is computed, so hard partisans tolerate off-position co-partisans.

SPATIAL PROXIMITY (salience-weighted): normalize salience s_i = g.salience[i]/sum_j g.salience[j]. Distance penalty D(g,c) = sum_i s_i * |effIdeal_i - c.positions[i]|^p, with p=2 (quadratic / Gaussian-like, default) selectable to p=1 (linear/tent). Spatial utility term Uspatial = -kSpatial * D(g,c), kSpatial≈2.5. Quadratic punishes extreme mismatches harder, matching real spatial-voting literature.

NAME RECOGNITION as a hard gate + soft penalty: awareness a = g.nameRecognition[c]. A group cannot meaningfully support an unknown candidate: gatedUtility = Uraw - kUnknown*(1-a), kUnknown≈4, AND the candidate is excluded from the softmax denominator when a < 0.05 (treated as not in consideration set). Recognition grows via ads/earned media: a' = a + (1-a)*reach*g.politicalInterest*kRec, kRec≈0.15 per exposure with diminishing returns built into the (1-a) factor.

FAVORABILITY & VALENCE: Uvalence = kVal*(c.valence - c.scandalLoad) + kFav*g.favorability[c]. kVal≈1.5, kFav≈2.0. Favorability is a slow affect term updated in opinion dynamics; valence is a fast quality term moved by debates/gaffes.

PARTISAN LOYALTY bonus: Uparty = kLoyal * g.partisanStrength * sign(match) where match=+1 if c.partyId===g.partyId, -1 if opposite major party, 0 if independent/third. kLoyal≈1.8. This is on top of the platform-pull on ideals, capturing tribal loyalty beyond policy.

IDENTITY / DESCRIPTIVE REPRESENTATION: Uidentity = kIdent * (fraction of axes where c.identityTags[axis]===g.tags[axis] weighted by axis affinity). kIdent≈0.4. Small but real co-ethnic/co-religious affinity.

INCUMBENCY & THERMOSTAT: Uincumbent = c.incumbent ? (kInc * (1 - kThermo*max(0,-g.mood)) ) : 0. Incumbents get a recognition/experience edge but a sour national mood (g.mood<0) erodes it (anti-incumbent thermostat). kInc≈0.6, kThermo≈1.2.
TOTAL UTILITY: U(g,c) = Uspatial + Uvalence + Uparty + Uidentity + Uincumbent - kUnknown*(1-a). All deterministic (no RNG) — reproducible given state.

VOTE CHOICE (multinomial logit / softmax): among the consideration set C(g) (candidates with a>=0.05), P(vote c | g, voted) = exp(beta*U(g,c)) / sum_{c' in C(g)} exp(beta*U(g,c')). beta = choice sensitivity ≈ 1.0..1.6; lower beta => more random/undecided, higher => sharper sorting. Undecided mass modeled by an implicit outside option utility U0 = kUndecided * (1 - maxFamiliarity) so low-info groups carry undecideds: P0 = exp(beta*U0)/(Z+exp(beta*U0)).

TURNOUT (logistic): let competitiveness comp in [0,1] from current latent margin (closer race => higher turnout). T(g) = sigma( a0 + a1*g.baseTurnoutPropensity*? ... ) concretely T(g) = 1/(1+exp(-( t0 + tProp*(2*g.baseTurnoutPropensity-1) + tInterest*(2*g.politicalInterest-1) + tComp*(2*comp-1) + tMobilize*mobilization_g + tEnthus*partisanEnthusiasm_g ))). Defaults t0=0.2, tProp=2.2, tInterest=1.4, tComp=0.8, tMobilize=1.0, tEnthus=0.7. mobilization_g raised by canvassing/GOTV targeting that group.

GROUP CONTRIBUTION: votesFor(c) = sum_g eligibleVoters * g.weight * T(g) * P(vote c|g). True latent share = votesFor(c)/sum_c votesFor(c). Turnout-weighted, so high-propensity groups count more — captures why electorate != adult population.

OPINION DYNAMICS — EXPONENTIAL SMOOTHING WITH INERTIA: each OpinionTick, every mutable scalar x moves toward a target x* by x' = x + lambda*(x* - x), lambda = baseInertia * issueVolatility (lambda≈0.05..0.25/week). Targets: favorability* driven by netAdTone_g + mediaTone reaching g via mediaDiet + endorsement bumps + scandal hits; economicSentiment* driven by EconomyIndicators (unemployment, real income, inflation) filtered by partisan motivated reasoning (co-partisans of governing party perceive economy better: bias = kMR*partisanAlignWithIncumbent); mood* drifts toward -k*timeInPowerOfIncumbentParty (thermostatic).

EVENT RESPONSE (RNG enters here): events (scandal, gaffe, viral ad, debate win, policy enactment) apply impulse deltas scaled by g.politicalInterest and mediaDiet overlap, plus gaussian noise from the seeded RNG. Scandal: favorability[c] -= scandalSeverity * (0.3+0.7*g.politicalInterest) * (oppositionAmplify); decays via the smoothing back toward baseline over subsequent ticks (so scandals fade unless reinforced).

CROSS-PRESSURE & PERSUADABILITY: crossPressure_g = clamp( spatialDistanceToOwnParty - spatialDistanceToOtherParty , 0,1 ); high cross-pressure raises effective lambda (more movable) and lowers partisanStrength's grip — these are the swing voters campaigns target.

POLLING SAMPLE & ERROR: true shares p_c computed as above. For a poll of n: model sampling error by drawing each reported share from a Dirichlet(alpha) with alpha_c = p_c * n_eff, n_eff = n / designEffect (designEffect≈1.5 for weighting/clustering). Reported MoE = z(0.95=1.96) * sqrt(p_max*(1-p_max)/n) * sqrt(designEffect). Then add houseEffect ~ Normal(pollsterLean, (1-quality)*0.03) toward that pollster's partisan tilt, and a coverage bias term for likely-voter screens. Undecided allocation and rounding to whole percents applied last.

LIKELY-VOTER SCREEN: 'LV' polls weight each group by T(g); 'RV' by registration propensity; 'Adults' by raw weight — so the same electorate yields different toplines by population model, a real and important lever.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT: evaluateElectorate and all utility/turnout/share math take NO rng. Only runOpinionTick (event noise) and conductPoll (sampling) accept an injected rng = rootRng.derive(streamId, tick). Same seed+inputs => identical outputs; tests assert byte-identical state hashes.

tddNotes: Determinism: evaluateElectorate(state, cands, ctx) called twice on a frozen state returns deep-equal results; runOpinionTick with the same seed+tick produces byte-identical state (hash equality).
Weights invariant: sum of group.weight === 1.0 within 1e-9 after init and after every opinion tick; eligibleVoters * sum(weights) preserved.
Softmax validity: for any group, sum over consideration set of P(vote c|g) + P_undecided === 1 within 1e-9; all P in [0,1].

Monotonic proximity: moving a candidate's position strictly closer to a group's effective ideal on a salient issue (others fixed) strictly increases that group's P(vote c) — assert with a perturbation test.
Salience matters: increasing salience on an issue where candidate is far should strictly decrease support; on an issue where candidate is close, increase it.
Name-rec gate: a candidate with nameRecognition[c]=0.0 receives ~0 votes and is excluded from softmax denominator; after applying ad reach, P(vote c) increases monotonically with awareness.
Turnout logistic bounds: T(g) in (0,1) for all finite inputs; higher baseTurnoutPropensity strictly raises T; higher competitiveness strictly raises T across all groups.
Partisan loyalty: a Strong-partisan group (partisanStrength=0.9) prefers its co-partisan over a spatially-closer opponent up to a quantifiable distance threshold; pure independents do not.
Thermostat: with incumbent of party P and group.mood negative, incumbent utility is lower than the same candidate as a non-incumbent — assert anti-incumbent erosion.
Motivated reasoning: given fixed EconomyIndicators, co-partisans of the governing party report higher economicSentiment* than out-partisans — assert sign of the gap equals kMR>0.
Opinion inertia: after a one-time favorability shock, favorability returns toward baseline over N ticks following geometric decay rate (1-lambda); assert half-life ≈ ln(2)/lambda.

Polling unbiasedness & MoE: over M=10000 seeded polls of the same state, mean reported share for a candidate equals true latent share within 3*SE; ~95% of polls' confidence intervals (estimate ± MoE) contain the true share (calibration test).
House effect direction: a pollster with pollsterLean>0 produces a mean topline biased toward the corresponding party relative to a zero-lean pollster on the same state.
LV vs Adults divergence: when high-propensity groups favor candidate A, the LV topline favors A more than the Adults topline on identical underlying state.
Serialization round-trip: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(electorateState)) is deep-equal to the original and produces identical evaluateElectorate output (no class instances / functions leak into state).
Consideration set in primaries: ctx.phase==='primary' for party 'dem' excludes Republican candidates from every group's softmax denominator.
Cross-pressure persuadability: a high-crossPressure group's favorability moves more per identical ad impulse than a low-crossPressure group (higher effective lambda).
risks: Group explosion: full cross-product of all demographic axes is combinatorially huge (10 axes => millions of intersections). Mitigation: synthesize only the top-N most-populous correlated intersections (target 50–400 groups) via a correlation matrix + iterative proportional fitting (raking) to match marginals; treat the long tail as a residual 'other' group. Must validate marginals still match within tolerance.

Parameter calibration: many k-coefficients (kSpatial, kLoyal, beta, turnout a-terms) must be tuned so outputs match real US benchmarks (e.g. ~90% partisan loyalty, realistic turnout by age). Risk of unrealistic results without a calibration harness and golden-state regression tests against known elections.

Double-counting affect: favorability is partly a function of the same spatial/party terms that already enter utility, risking feedback loops. Mitigation: keep favorability as an independent slow affect channel fed by events/media only, not re-derived from spatial distance each tick.
Softmax scale sensitivity: beta too high => deterministic landslides and zero undecideds; too low => everyone 50/50. Needs guardrails and tests pinning beta's effect on undecided share.
Motivated-reasoning + thermostat interaction could produce runaway or oscillating mood. Mitigation: clamp all [-1,1] state, bound lambda, add tests for stability over 200 ticks (no NaN/divergence).

Polling calibration: getting MoE coverage to truly hit 95% requires correct design-effect and Dirichlet alpha; naive Normal approximation under-covers near 0/1 shares. Mitigation: Dirichlet sampling + calibration test in TDD list.

Performance at scale: evaluating every group×candidate every campaign tick across thousands of down-ballot races. Mitigation: only evaluate the player's active jurisdiction(s) at full fidelity; background jurisdictions use a cheap aggregate model and lazy promotion.

Modding safety: data-driven issues/axes mean malformed JSON could break invariants (weights not summing to 1, unknown issue ids). Mitigation: a validation/normalization pass on load that rakes weights and fills missing positions from party platform.

designs.subsystem: Campaign Engine — candidate attributes, data-driven campaign actions, tycoon layer (offices/staff/strategy), fundraising & budget, and the action→electorate effect pipeline, scheduled over a campaign calendar.
designs.overview:
This subsystem (`src/engine/campaign/`) is the pure-TS layer a player uses to run for a single office. It is deterministic, DOM-free, and JSON-serializable. It does NOT own the electorate (voter groups, favorability math, vote tallies) — that belongs to the electorate-sim subsystem. Instead it produces a typed stream of `ElectorateEffect` objects that the electorate-sim consumes, and it reads back read-only snapshots (polls, segment sizes) the electorate-sim exposes. The boundary is the `CampaignEngineContext` injected at construction: `{ rng: SeededRng; calendar: GameCalendar; electorate: ElectorateReadModel; emitEffect(e: ElectorateEffect): void; }`. This keeps the campaign engine unit-testable in isolation with a mock electorate.

Engine/UI split: the engine exposes (1) pure reducers `applyCampaignAction(state, cmd, ctx) -> {state, effects, log}` and `tickCampaign(state, ctx) -> {state, effects, log}`; (2) pure selectors `selectAffordableActions`, `selectStaffEffectiveness`, `selectBurnRate`, `selectProjectedCashOnHand`, `selectDaysToElection`. React never mutates state; it dispatches `CampaignCommand`s and renders selectors. All randomness flows through `ctx.rng` (a splittable seeded PRNG) so a save+replay of the command log is bit-identical.

Data-driven core: every campaign action, staff role, office-tier, ad channel, donor class, and endorsement type is a `*Def` record loaded from `src/data/campaign/*.ts` and referenced by stable string id. Engine logic is generic over these defs; designers add content (a new ad channel, a new staff role, a Super PAC archetype) by adding data, not code. Defs carry their cost/effect/cooldown/diminishing-returns parameters as plain numbers so they are moddable and serializable.

Time model: the campaign runs on a daily tick from `campaignStartDay` to `electionDay`. Each tick advances `daysElapsed`, accrues passive small-dollar income, pays daily-prorated salaries, applies action decay/inertia, processes the scheduled-action queue for that day, and decays name-recognition/favorability momentum back toward baseline. Player actions are either INSTANT (resolved this tick) or SCHEDULED (placed on a future day, consuming staff capacity and budget at resolution). Action Points / staff capacity gate how much can happen per day; money gates the rest.

Effect pipeline (the heart): an action def declares raw `EffectSpec`s in canonical units. At resolution the engine computes `magnitude = base * staffMult * officePresenceMult * strategyMult * diminishingReturns(history) * rng.jitter() * fatiguePenalty`, scales reach by targeted segment sizes from the electorate read model, then emits `ElectorateEffect`s (nameRecognitionDelta, favorabilityDelta per segment, turnoutPropensityDelta, persuasionPressure). The electorate-sim integrates these with its own inertia, so the campaign engine never writes voter numbers directly.

mechanics: EFFECTIVENESS MULTIPLIER CHAIN: every action's realized magnitude = baseMagnitude * candidateSkillMult * staffMult * officePresenceMult * strategyMult * drMult * fatigueMult * rngJitter. Each factor is a bounded float; the chain is multiplicative so weaknesses compound. candidateSkillMult depends on action.kind: rallies/speeches use charisma, debates use 0.5*oratory+0.3*competence+0.2*charisma, policy announcements use competence*clarity, fundraising uses fundraisingAbility. Map a 0..100 attribute to a multiplier via attrMult(a)=0.6+0.008*a (so 50->1.0, 100->1.4, 0->0.6).

DIMINISHING RETURNS: drMult(n) where n = count of same-kind uses on same target within the curve window. Use saturating exponential: drMult = drCurve.floor + (1-drCurve.floor)*exp(-drCurve.k * priorEffectiveUses). priorEffectiveUses decays with time: each prior use contributes exp(-ln2*daysAgo/drCurve.halfLifeDays). Typical: rallies k=0.35 floor=0.15 halfLife=10; TV ad in a market k=0.18 floor=0.25 halfLife=7 (frequency capping); door-knocking k=0.05 floor=0.5 halfLife=30 (slow saturation, ground game stays valuable).

NAME RECOGNITION GROWTH (logistic toward 1.0): for a broad-reach action, nameRecDelta_segment = (1 - currentNameRec_segment) * reachFraction * magnitude * 0.6. The (1-current) term gives automatic diminishing returns as recognition saturates. Targeted actions multiply reachFraction by the segment's strategy weight and the segment's share of population.

FAVORABILITY: positive actions push favorability among reached & already-aware voters: favDelta = magnitude * awareFraction * (1 - tone_penalty) where awareFraction = currentNameRec_segment (you can't persuade who doesn't know you). Net contrast/attack: a fraction (0.4+0.4*|tone|) of magnitude routes to opponentFavorability as a negative delta, the rest to own favorability, but backlash subtracts magnitude*backlashCoeff from own favorability when tone>0.6, scaled by (1-integrity/100) and by target-segment's attackAversion.

TURNOUT/GOTV: GOTV and canvassing emit turnoutPropensity deltas only among already-supportive segments (electorate read model exposes leanSupport per segment): turnoutDelta = magnitude * supportShare * groundGameMult, where groundGameMult = 1 + 0.5*(totalFieldCapacityUtilization). GOTV effects are front-loaded near election day via lag.onsetDays small; the engine multiplies GOTV magnitude by gotvWindowMult = clamp((14 - daysToElection)/14, 0, 1) so it's near-useless 3 months out, full power in the final 2 weeks.

ADVERTISING REACH & TARGETING: a buy of spendCents in channel c reaches reachFraction = channelDef.cpmReach * (spendCents / channelDef.referenceSpendCents), capped by channelDef.maxReachPerFlight and subject to frequency-cap DR. Digital allows segment targeting (precision 0.85), TV is broad with demographic skew vectors per program-genre, mail is geo-targeted (precision 0.95) but slow (lag.onsetDays=3), radio cheap+narrow. Attack ads set the EffectSpec.tone high and route more magnitude to opponentFavorability.

STAFF EFFECTIVENESS: staffMult for an action = 1 + sum over relevant staff of (effectivenessMultiplier-baseline)*roleWeight, capped per role. effectivenessMultiplier = 0.5 + 0.005*skill * moraleFactor * (1 - 0.004*fatigue), moraleFactor = 0.7 + 0.006*morale. A pollster doesn't boost rallies but improves targeting accuracy (reduces wasted reach: effectiveReach = reach*(0.6+0.4*pollsterQuality)). A campaign manager applies a global org-wide multiplier 1+0.002*skill to ALL capacities.

MORALE DYNAMICS (per tick): morale += moraleDrift where moraleDrift = 0.15*(payFairness-0.5)*2 + 0.1*momentum*100scaled + 0.1*(winProbTrend) - 0.08*overworkPressure, clamped, then nudged toward 50 by 0.05 mean-reversion. payFairness = clamp(salary / marketRate(role,skill), 0,1.5). Morale<30 triggers attrition roll each week: P(quit)= (30-morale)/100 * (1-loyalty).

OFFICE PRESENCE: officePresenceMult for a geo-targeted action in region r = 1 + sum of active offices' presenceMultiplier-1 in r and adjacent regions (adjacency weight 0.3), where each office's presenceMultiplier ramps: effective = 1 + (tierMax-1)*clamp((day-openedOnDay)/rampDays,0,1). Field capacity from organizers only counts if housed in an office within range of the target region.

FUNDRAISING — SMALL DOLLAR: an email/online ask yields = smallDollar.reservoirCents * askEfficiency * enthusiasm * fundraiserStaffMult * drMult, where askEfficiency≈0.02 per ask, enthusiasm = clamp(1 + momentum, 0.2, 2.0). Reservoir depletes by yield and refreshes at refreshPerDayCents (refresh scales with nameRecognition & small-dollar list size). Big news moments (debate win, viral moment) spike reservoir via a momentum->reservoir injection.

FUNDRAISING — CALL TIME / LARGE DONOR: a call-time block consumes candidate AP+stamina, yields = min(prospectsWorked*avgGiftCents*relationshipQuality*fundraisingAbilityMult, remaining individual-limit headroom). Each gift checks contributionLimits; over-limit portion auto-refunded and logged as complianceFlag. relationshipQuality rises 0.03 per finance event.

FUNDRAISING — EVENTS & PACs: a fundraising EVENT def has ticketTierCents, capacity, and a hostQuality; gross = capacity * ticketTier * sellThrough(hostQuality, relationshipQuality) minus eventCostCents; net can be negative if poorly attended. PAC asks unlock at favorWith>=threshold and pay maxHardMoneyCents-givenCents; courting a PAC raises favorWith but may add stringsAttached creating flip-flop/integrity risk.

SUPER PAC (independent expenditure): SuperPacState runs its own ad flights the campaign CANNOT legally coordinate — engine models it as an autonomous emitter aligned to the candidate's ideologyVector; player can only influence via public 'message signaling' actions. Coordination attempts raise complianceFlags with a scandal-spawn probability gated by (1-integrity/100).

BURN RATE & PROJECTION: burnRateCents7d = sum(expense ledger, last 7 days)/7. selectProjectedCashOnHand(day) = cashOnHand - committedSpend - burnRateCents7d*(electionDay-day) + projectedIncome(day..election). projectedIncome integrates small-dollar refresh + scheduled events. UI warns when projected COH<0 before election day (the classic 'going dark' failure).

ROI: each action logs realized aggregate effect (sum |magnitude| weighted by segment value) and its cost; selectActionROI = effectScore/costCents. Used by AI rivals and surfaced to the player to compare e.g. TV vs digital vs ground.

SCANDAL / OPPO RESEARCH: an oppo-research action against opponent rolls against their latent ScandalRecords: P(dig)=baseDigChance*researcherSkill*(1-target.integrity/200); on success flips a latent scandal toward public, queued as a future attack-ad payload. The candidate's own integrity reduces own gaffeProneness; high-tempo + low stamina raises per-action gaffe roll P(gaffe)=gaffeProneness*(1+fatigueFactor)*(stamina<30?1.5:1).

ACTION POINTS & STAMINA: actionPointsToday resets each tick to base 3 + (mediaPosture bonus) + campaignManager bonus. Candidate-present actions draw AP and stamina; staff-only actions (staff-run phone bank, ad placement by comms team) draw org capacity but 0 AP, enabling parallelism — the tycoon payoff is doing many things per day via staff while the candidate's personal time stays scarce.

TICK ORDER (deterministic): (1) advance day; (2) accrue small-dollar refresh & passive earned media; (3) pay prorated salaries & rent, update burn rate; (4) regen stamina, decay fatigue, drift morale, run weekly attrition on day%7; (5) ramp offices; (6) decay cooldowns & momentum (momentum *= 0.92 toward 0); (7) resolve all ScheduledActions with resolveDay==today in stable instanceId order; (8) emit pending lagged ElectorateEffects; (9) recompute derived selectors. RNG is split per-step via rng.fork(stepId+day) so reordering UI never changes outcomes.

tddNotes: DETERMINISM: running tickCampaign N times from the same seeded state + same command log produces byte-identical CampaignState (deep-equal JSON). Reordering two independent same-day INSTANT actions yields identical final state because each draws from rng.fork(stepId+day) not the shared stream.

DIMINISHING RETURNS MONOTONICITY: for a rally def, the realized nameRecognition magnitude of the k-th consecutive same-segment rally within the DR window is strictly less than the (k-1)-th (drMult strictly decreasing), and drMult never goes below drCurve.floor.

NAME-REC SATURATION: repeatedly applying a name-recognition action drives a segment's nameRecognition asymptotically toward 1.0 and never exceeds 1.0 (logistic (1-current) factor); delta per application strictly decreases.

FEC LIMIT ENFORCEMENT: a call-time action that would push an individual donor past contributionLimits.perIndividualPrimaryCents credits only the headroom, refunds the remainder, raises exactly one 'over-individual-limit' ComplianceFlag, and cashOnHand increases by exactly the capped amount (ledger balances: sum of income-expense == cashOnHand).

LEDGER INTEGRITY: after any sequence of ticks/actions, cashOnHand === sum(ledger income) - sum(ledger expense), and committedSpend === sum(reservedCostCents of scheduled+unresolved actions). No money created or destroyed off-ledger.

BURN/PROJECTION: with zero income and a fixed weeklyPayroll, selectProjectedCashOnHand decreases linearly and selectDaysUntilBroke matches cashOnHand/(dailyBurn) within rounding; a campaign hits 'went-dark' failure exactly when projected COH crosses 0 before electionDay.

GOTV WINDOW: a GOTV action scheduled 60 days out produces ~0 turnoutPropensity effect (gotvWindowMult≈0); the identical action 3 days out produces near-full magnitude; assert the ratio matches clamp((14-d)/14).

STAMINA/AP GATING: an action requiring candidate presence fails (returns CommandError 'insufficient-stamina' or 'insufficient-action-points') without mutating state when stamina/AP are below cost; a staff-only action with 0 AP still succeeds, proving parallelism.

CAPACITY RESERVATION: scheduling an action reserves capacity & cash now (committedSpend rises, capacity available drops); cancelling it restores both exactly; a second action that would exceed remaining capacity on the same resolveDay is rejected.

MORALE→ATTRITION: a staffer paid far below market trends to low morale over weeks and eventually triggers a quit roll; with loyalty=1 the quit probability is 0 (loyalty gates attrition); high pay keeps morale>=50.

STRATEGY TARGETING CONSERVATION: with segment-targeted strategy, summed reach across segments equals the broad reach of the same action (targeting reallocates, not inflates, reach); a pollster increases the fraction of reach landing on intended segments.

ATTACK BACKLASH: an attack action (tone>0.6) by a low-integrity candidate produces a larger own-favorability backlash than the same action by a high-integrity candidate; opponentFavorability delta is negative in both cases.

OFFICE RAMP: presenceMultiplier of a freshly opened office equals 1.0 on openedOnDay and reaches tierMax exactly at openedOnDay+rampDays, linearly; geo-targeted action efficacy in that region rises accordingly.
SCHEDULING ORDER: scheduled actions on the same resolveDay resolve in ascending instanceId order regardless of insertion order, guaranteeing deterministic emitted-effect sequence.

DATA-DRIVEN GENERICITY: adding a new CampaignActionDef to the data file (no engine code change) makes it dispatchable, schedulable, and correctly cost/cooldown/DR-tracked; a test loads a synthetic def and asserts the reducer handles it.
SERIALIZATION ROUND-TRIP: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(state)) deep-equals state (no Maps/Sets/functions/NaN/Infinity in serialized state; SegmentMaps are plain records, money is integer cents).
risks: Boundary leakage: the campaign engine must NOT compute final vote totals or own voter favorability state — only emit ElectorateEffects. If it caches nameRecognition (for projection) the cache can desync from electorate-sim's authoritative copy; mitigate by treating the cache as advisory and refreshing from ctx.electorate each tick.
Float drift in money: use integer cents everywhere; a single float dollar amount can break ledger-integrity invariants over thousands of ticks.

RNG coupling: if any action reads the shared rng stream directly instead of a forked sub-stream, action reordering in the UI changes outcomes and breaks determinism tests — enforce rng.fork(stepId+day) discipline.

Multiplier-chain explosion: stacking staff+office+strategy+momentum multipliers unclamped can produce absurd single-action effects; every factor needs an explicit cap and the final magnitude should be clamped to a per-channel ceiling.
Diminishing-returns window bookkeeping is O(history); cap actionHistory length / use a rolling per-(kind,target) aggregate so late-game ticks stay fast.

Balance/realism: real campaigns are dominated by paid media + ground game timing; if DR/curves are mistuned the optimal strategy collapses to one action (e.g. spam rallies). Curve constants must live in data for tuning without code changes.

Super PAC non-coordination is legally/thematically important; modeling it as a fully autonomous emitter is simplest but players will want influence — the 'message signaling' channel must be carefully bounded to avoid trivializing the firewall.
Combinatorial AI: AI rivals using selectActionROI greedily can be exploitable or degenerate; needs a stochastic/portfolio layer (out of scope here but the ROI selector is the hook).
Calendar/stage transitions (primary->general) reset contribution limit headroom and swap electorate composition; forgetting to reset per-stage limit counters is a common correctness bug.

designs.overview:
This subsystem lives in `@engine/governing/*` as pure, deterministic TypeScript — no DOM, no I/O, no `Date.now()`. All randomness flows through the engine's seeded RNG (`Rng` interface: `nextFloat()`, `nextInt(min,max)`, `fork(salt: string)`), and every legislator decision uses a forked RNG keyed by `(billId, legislatorId, stageId, tick)` so replays are bit-identical. The engine exposes a single reducer-style entrypoint `advanceLegislation(state: GovState, ctx: SimContext, actions: GovAction[]): { state: GovState; events: GovEvent[] }`, called each calendar tick by the master engine loop. The UI never mutates `GovState`; it reads selectors and dispatches `GovAction`s (introduce bill, assign committee, schedule markup, offer amendment, cast player vote, open negotiation, issue executive order, sign/veto). 

The core abstraction is the **legislative process as a configurable state machine** authored in data: a `LegislativeProcess` is an array of `ProcessStage` nodes with typed `gates` (vote thresholds, committee approval, calendar scheduling) and `transitions` (success/fail/amend/table edges). A bill is an instance walking that machine; the same machine code drives the US House+Senate (bicameral, conference), Nebraska (unicameral, nonpartisan), 49 bicameral state legislatures, city councils (ordinances), ballot initiatives (signature → ballot → referendum), and executive orders (single-actor fast path). Jurisdiction differences are pure data: `Chamber[]`, `vetoOverrideFraction`, `germanenessRules`, `committeeSystem`, `filibusterEnabled`, term lengths.

Bills are fully data-driven and modder-authorable: a `Bill` is a title + sponsors + ordered `Provision[]`, where each provision carries `EffectOp[]` describing deltas to simulation values, budget line items, group-targeted impacts, and situation triggers, plus optional `eligibilityConditions` and a CBO-style `FiscalNote` computed deterministically from the effects. Provisions are the unit of amendment (strike/insert/modify/substitute), so amendments are first-class data, not special-cased.

Legislators are AI agents (`Legislator`) with `ideologyVector` (multi-axis), `party`, `partyLoyalty`, `districtProfile` (the demographic/economic makeup they answer to), `reelectionPressure`, and `traits`. Vote prediction (whip count) is a deterministic utility model: each legislator computes `utility(bill)` from ideological congruence + district interest + party pressure + leadership/whip pressure + logrolled favors + constituent salience, mapped through a logistic to a YEA probability, then thresholded (with a seeded jitter draw) to a predicted/actual position. Negotiation is modeled as concrete `Deal` objects (amendment concessions, earmarks, future-vote IOUs, committee favors) that mutate legislator utilities; logrolling is a matching algorithm over vote-IOUs.

Enacted policy feeds back into the electorate/economy sim via `EffectOp`s scheduled onto a global `EffectLedger` with per-effect **lag** (rampStartTick, rampDurationTicks, decayHalfLifeTicks) so impacts phase in/out smoothly à la Democracy 4 inertia. The governing engine itself only *emits* these scheduled effects and credits/blames the responsible actor; the electorate, economy, and situation subsystems consume the ledger. The executive side models `ExecutiveOffice` (president/governor/mayor) powers — sign/veto/line-item-veto/pocket-veto, executive orders, agency directives, and budget proposal/impoundment — as actions that either create bills, short-circuit the machine, or schedule effects directly, all gated by the same data-driven `power` definitions per jurisdiction.

mechanics: LEGISLATOR VOTE UTILITY (core whip model). For legislator L on bill B: utility = wIdeo*ideoCongruence + wDistrict*districtInterest + wParty*partyPressure + wWhip*whipPressure + wFavor*favorTerm + wExec*execPressure − controversyPenalty. ideoCongruence = 1 − (cosineDistance(L.ideologyVector, B.ideologyVector)) ∈ [0,1] then re-centered to [-1,1] as (2*congruence−1). Trait weights override base w* (e.g. firebrand: wIdeo×1.5, wParty×0.6; institutionalist: wParty×1.4).

DISTRICT INTEREST TERM. districtInterest = Σ over B.provisions p of provisionDistrictValue(p, L.districtProfile), where provisionDistrictValue projects p.effects' groupHappiness/economy targets onto the district's demographic weights. Earmarks targeting L.districtId add a fixed +earmarkBonus. Scaled by L.reelectionPressure so it dominates near elections.

PARTY & WHIP PRESSURE. partyPressure = L.partyLoyalty * partyLineStance(B) where partyLineStance ∈ [-1,1] is the caucus position (computed from leadership ideology + party platform vs B.ideologyVector). whipPressure adds the leadership's targeted lean on this bill: whipPressure = whipIntensity(B) * leadershipRelationship(L) and is what 'spending political capital' raises.

YEA PROBABILITY. p_yea = logistic(k * utility + bias) with k≈4.0 (sharpness) and bias from L.traits (maverick lowers predictability via larger jitter). Predicted position = p_yea>0.5 ? 'yea':'nay'; whip count aggregates p_yea (expected yeas = Σ p_yea) and also a worst/best case band (Σ over draws). ACTUAL vote draws u=rng.fork(billId,L.id,stageId).nextFloat(); yea iff u < p_yea. Abstain if |utility|<abstainThreshold AND not party-whipped.

VOTE RESOLUTION & THRESHOLDS. A StageGate of type 'vote' has: tallyBasis ('present'|'fullBody'), threshold (0.5 simple, 0.6 supermajority, 0.667 veto-override / constitutional-amendment, 0.75 some local), tieBreaker ('vp'|'speaker'|'fail'|'mayor'). Pass iff yeas / basis ≥ threshold. Quorum checked first; below quorum → no vote, dwell++.

FILIBUSTER / CLOTURE (US Senate floor only). If stage.allowsFilibuster and bill controversy>filibusterThreshold and minority size≥41% of 100, a cloture sub-gate (threshold 0.6 = 60 votes) is inserted before the simple-majority passage vote. Failing cloture → transition 'table'. Reconciliation/EO/most state chambers set allowsFilibuster=false.

COMMITTEE MARKUP. On entering committee: route by max IssueTag overlap (bill.topicTags ∩ committee.jurisdictionTopics). Chair decides via chairPriority = utility(chair,B) − backlogPressure; if below pocketThreshold the chair pockets it (no scheduling) until a discharge petition reaches committee.dischargePetitionThreshold of full chamber. Markup runs an amendment phase (AI offers amendments to raise its own caucus's utility) then a committee vote (same vote mechanics, basis=committee members).

AMENDMENTS AS DATA. An Amendment = {type:'strike'|'insert'|'modify'|'substitute', targetProvisionId?, newProvision?, sponsorId}. Applying mutates bill.provisions, then RE-DERIVES bill.ideologyVector and bill.fiscalNote (pure functions deriveIdeology(provisions), deriveFiscalNote(provisions, jurisdiction)). Poison-pill detection: if an adopted amendment moves bill.ideologyVector cosine-distance from sponsor's vector beyond poisonThreshold, sponsor's support flips (models 'killer amendments').

NEGOTIATION / LOGROLLING. When a whip count predicts failure within margin closeable by deals, proposer (exec or floor leader, or player action) generates candidate Deals targeting pivotal undecided legislators (those with |utility| minimal). matchLogroll(): pairs legislators A,B who each have a bill the other is pivotal on, creating reciprocal future-vote-ious; accept iff bothUtilityGain>0 and within corruptibility/loyalty constraints. Accepting a Deal applies utilityDelta and, for earmarks, inserts considerationProvision (which re-scores the FiscalNote — pork costs money).

POLITICAL CAPITAL. Executive pressure and whip operations cost politicalCapital (capitalCost per Deal/pressure op). Capital regenerates +regenPerTick scaled by approvalRating; depleted capital makes the bully pulpit ineffective. Player governing loop is largely capital-allocation.

EFFECT SCHEDULING & LAG (feedback into sim). On reaching terminalSuccessStage, for each provision effect e: push ScheduledEffect{ effectOp:e, enactedTick:tick, agencyCapacityMult: implementingAgency?.capacity ?? 1 }. Per tick, appliedMagnitude(t) = e.magnitude * agencyCapacityMult * ramp(t) * decay(t) where ramp(t)=clamp((t − enacted − rampStart)/rampDuration,0,1) and decay(t)= e.decayHalfLife? 0.5^((t−enacted−rampStart−rampDuration)/decayHalfLife):1, zeroed after sunsetTick. The electorate/economy subsystems read the ledger's current applied deltas — governing only writes them.

ATTRIBUTION / ELECTORAL FEEDBACK. Each ScheduledEffect carries attributionActorId. As group happiness/economy move, the electorate sim credits/blames that actor, adjusting their approvalInDistrict and (at election time) vote share — closing the loop with the campaign subsystem. Salient (high-controversy) enacted bills produce larger attribution swings.

EXECUTIVE ACTION FAST PATH. Executive-order process has a single 'executive-action' stage gated only by power-availability and (optionally) a legality check (Condition list); on pass it schedules effects immediately but with shorter durability (decayHalfLife smaller, easily reversible by successor EO or court situation trigger). Line-item veto (where power exists) strikes individual budgetItems/provisions before signing rather than rejecting whole bill.

VETO & OVERRIDE. At executive-action stage for statutes: exec computes signUtility = ideoCongruence(exec,bill) + partyAlignment − fiscalConcern. If signUtility<vetoThreshold → veto (creates vetoMessage, transition→veto-override stage). Override stage runs a vote with threshold = jurisdiction.vetoOverrideFraction (federal 2/3, many states 2/3, some 3/5 or simple majority). Pocket veto if session ends within pocketWindow and exec declines to sign.

BALLOT INITIATIVE PATH. kind 'ballot-initiative' uses a process: signature-gathering gate (threshold = required signatures as fraction of last turnout, accumulated via player campaign actions) → ballot-qualification → electorate-vote stage (venue 'electorate', the electorate sim returns y/n by simulating voters as on a candidate, using bill.ideologyVector and group impacts) → enacted. Bypasses legislature and executive entirely.

STALENESS / SINE DIE. Each tick, bills with (tick − lastActionTick) > stalenessLimit in session-based calendars are at risk; at sineDieTick all non-enacted bills in session-based jurisdictions transition to 'died-' terminal unless carryover=true. Continuous calendars (most city councils) never sine-die.

tddNotes: determinism: running advanceLegislation twice from the same seeded GovState+actions yields byte-identical GovState and identical GovEvent[] (deep-equal). The same bill scored by deriveFiscalNote twice returns identical netDeficitImpact arrays.
id stability: generateId only ever uses state.rngCounter (incremented), never Math.random/Date.now — assert two ids generated from cloned state are equal.
whip count monotonicity: increasing whipPressure (spending political capital) on a bill never decreases expected yeas; expectedYeas is non-decreasing in whipIntensity.
logistic vote prob: p_yea(utility=0)≈0.5; p_yea→1 as utility→+∞, →0 as utility→−∞; symmetric around 0 when bias=0.
threshold passing: a vote with 60 yeas / 100 present passes a 0.5 and 0.6 gate but fails 0.667; tieBreaker 'fail' makes a 50/50 split fail, 'vp' makes it pass.
committee routing: a bill tagged ['taxes'] routes to Ways & Means / Finance (max jurisdictionTopics overlap), not Judiciary; tie broken deterministically by committee id ordering.
pocket veto / chair gatekeeping: a chair whose utility(bill) < pocketThreshold leaves the bill in markupQueue indefinitely until a discharge petition ≥ threshold transitions it out.

amendment re-derivation: applying a 'strike' amendment that removes a spending provision reduces fiscalNote.totalOutlays and shifts bill.ideologyVector measurably; a non-severable strike sets status to failed.
poison pill: inserting a provision that pushes bill.ideologyVector beyond poisonThreshold from the sponsor flips sponsor support (predicted position nay) — assert the flip occurs at the boundary.
filibuster gate: a controversial Senate bill with a 41-seat minority must clear a 0.6 cloture sub-gate before the 0.5 passage vote; with allowsFilibuster=false the cloture gate is absent.
Nebraska unicameral: a state-NE statute process has chambers=['state-NE-unicameral'], no second-chamber stage, no conference, party='NP' for all members so partyPressure term is ~0.
veto override: a vetoed federal statute requires ≥2/3 in BOTH chambers; passing 2/3 in one but not the other leaves status vetoed (not overridden).
effect lag math: a ScheduledEffect with rampStart=2,rampDuration=4,magnitude=10 contributes 0 at t=enacted+1, 0 at +2, 2.5 at +3, 5 at +4, 10 at +6, and (with halfLife=8) ≈5 at +14.
sunset & decay: an effect with sunsetTick produces 0 applied magnitude strictly after sunsetTick; with decayHalfLife null it stays at full magnitude forever post-ramp.
attribution: enacting a bill schedules effects all carrying attributionActorId === sponsorId; the electorate subsystem reading the ledger can sum blame/credit per actor.
executive order durability: an EO-scheduled effect has shorter decayHalfLife than the equivalent statute effect and is removable by a successor EO action (effect ledger entry tagged reversible=true).

sine die: in a session-based jurisdiction, a bill with no action past sineDieTick transitions to died-sine-die unless its process.calendarModel carries it over; continuous-calendar bills never die this way.

ballot initiative: a ballot-initiative reaching the electorate-vote stage is resolved by the electorate sim (not legislators); accumulating signatures below threshold by qualification deadline transitions to failed.
risks: Coupling leak: the temptation to read electorate/economy state directly inside vote utility. Mitigation: legislators consume only a denormalized DistrictProfile snapshot refreshed by the master loop, not live cross-subsystem reads, preserving the engine/UI and inter-subsystem decoupling.

Performance: a full US-federal whip count is 535 legislators × N active bills × per-tick; naive recompute is costly. Mitigation: cache utility per (bill, legislator) keyed on a versioned hash of (bill.ideologyVector, deals, whipIntensity); only recompute on invalidation.

Determinism foot-guns: any iteration over Record<> in nondeterministic key order, or floating-point summation order differences, breaks replay. Mitigation: always sort ids before iterating; use a fixed reduction order; centralize all RNG through forked salts.

Balance/realism: logistic sharpness k and the w* weights heavily determine whether the chamber feels gridlocked or rubber-stamp. Mitigation: expose them as tunable data constants and cover with characterization tests against known historical pass-rate targets.

Data authoring burden: 535 federal + ~7400 state + thousands of local legislators is a lot of data. Mitigation: generate legislators procedurally from district demographics + seeded ideology with a thin curated override layer for real notable figures.
Combinatorial deal space: naive logroll matching is O(bills² × legislators²). Mitigation: restrict candidate deals to pivotal legislators (|utility|<margin) and cap deals per tick.

Mod safety: user-authored EffectOps could destabilize the sim (runaway magnitudes). Mitigation: validate effects against per-target magnitude clamps and a schema validator at load; reject or clamp out-of-range modded bills.

designs.subsystem: Simulation Core — time/calendar, deterministic RNG, event queue, Democracy-style effects graph, game-state shape, reducer/dispatch, and JSON save/load (the engine contract all other subsystems plug into)
designs.overview: This subsystem is the deterministic spine of Stateline. It lives entirely under `src/engine/core/` as pure TypeScript (no DOM, no I/O, no Date.now, no Math.random) and exposes a single contract — the `Engine` facade — that the React/Zustand UI and every other subsystem (campaign, governance, demographics, AI) consume read-only. The root object is `GameState`, a plain JSON-serializable tree advanced by `engine.tick()` over a discrete game `Calendar`. Determinism is total: every stochastic decision draws from a seeded `RngState` (mulberry32 core, splitmix64 seed-mixing for per-system substreams), so a given `(saveVersion, rootSeed, action log)` always replays byte-identical state. The four pillars are: (1) CALENDAR/TICK — a day-granular clock where campaign mode ticks by day and governing mode fast-forwards week/month, with future-dated work held in a binary-heap `EventQueue` keyed by `dayIndex`; (2) RNG — `createRng(seed)` plus `forkRng(parent, label)` giving each system an independent reproducible stream; (3) EVENTS — a unified queue of scheduled deterministic events (election day, debate, payday, bill votes) and seeded random events (scandals, economic shocks, news cycles) gated by per-tick hazard rolls and cooldowns; (4) EFFECTS GRAPH — a Democracy-4-style directed weighted graph of `SimNode`s (sim values, policies, situations, voter-group attributes) connected by `SimEdge`s with transfer functions and inertia, evaluated each tick by a fixed-iteration relaxation pass over a precomputed topological order with feedback-loop damping. State mutation flows through a pure reducer `applyAction(state, action, ctx) -> state` (structural-sharing immutable update) and a `tickReducer`. Save/load is `serialize(state) -> string` / `deserialize(json) -> GameState` with an integer `schemaVersion` and an ordered migration chain. The design is data-driven: nodes, edges, event definitions, and action handlers are registered from `@data/*` content packs at `createGame` time into an immutable `ContentRegistry`, so the same engine code runs any modded ruleset. Engine code is split engine-logic vs UI: the engine never imports React; the UI never mutates state except via `engine.dispatch(action)`.

coreEntities.name: RngState

seed: number — original seed this stream was created from (kept for debugging/replay clarity)
label: string — human-readable provenance e.g. 'events' or 'graph.noise@tick=140' (debug only)
relationships: createRng(seed): RngState; nextU32(rng) mutates s and returns uint32; nextFloat (0..1), nextRange(lo,hi), nextInt, chance(p), pick(arr), shuffle(arr) all built on nextU32
forkRng(parent, salt: string|number): RngState — derives a child seed = splitmix64(parent.seed ^ hash(salt)); used so each system/tick gets an independent stream WITHOUT consuming the parent
Long-lived streams stored in GameState.rngStreams; ephemeral per-tick streams forked fresh each tick from a stable salt (tickCount) and discarded

coreEntities.name: SimNode (data) + node runtime value
coreEntities.purpose: A node in the Democracy-style effects graph: a simulation value, policy, situation, or voter-group attribute. The DEFINITION is immutable content; the VALUE lives in GraphState.values.
keyFields: id: string — stable unique key e.g. 'sim.unemployment', 'policy.carbonTax', 'situation.recession', 'group.suburbanWomen.turnout'
kind: SimNodeKind — 'simValue' | 'policy' | 'situation' | 'groupAttr' | 'input'
min: number — clamp floor (usually 0)
max: number — clamp ceiling (usually 1; values are normalized 0..1 internally, display-scaled in UI)
baseValue: number — equilibrium/default the node relaxes toward when no inputs (homeostasis)
inertia: number — 0..1 smoothing; nextValue = lerp(target, prevValue, inertia); high inertia = slow change (economy slow, news fast)
volatility: number — stddev of optional per-tick gaussian noise added (0 = fully deterministic-from-inputs)
activeThreshold: number | null — for situations: situation is 'active' when value crosses this (drives event hazards)
tags: string[] — e.g. ['economic'],['social'] for UI grouping and edge targeting
relationships: Connected by SimEdge in/out lists; GraphState.values[id] holds current number; GraphState.targets[id] holds last computed pre-inertia target
policy nodes are set directly by player actions (e.g. setPolicyLevel) and act as graph inputs
situation nodes can spawn events when crossing activeThreshold

coreEntities.name: SimEdge (data)
coreEntities.purpose: A directed weighted causal link source->target with a transfer function, implementing Democracy-4 style 'X affects Y by amount, with lag'.
keyFields: id: string — `${from}->${to}`
from: string — source node id
to: string — target node id
weight: number — signed strength (e.g. +0.4 means high source pushes target up; -0.3 inverse)
transfer: TransferKind — 'linear' | 'multiplier' | 'sigmoid' | 'step' | 'inverse'; how source value maps to its contribution
lag: number — ticks of delay before influence reaches target (implemented via per-edge ring buffer of recent source values)
curve: number — shaping exponent/steepness param for sigmoid/step (default 1)
relationships: Aggregated per target: target_input = baseValue + Σ_edges transferFn(edgeWeight, delayedSourceValue); then clamped + inertia applied
Edges may form cycles (economy<->confidence); handled by RELAXATION not strict topo (see mechanics)

coreEntities.name: GameEvent (queued) + EventDef (data)
coreEntities.purpose: Unit of scheduled or random happening. EventDef is the immutable template; GameEvent is a concrete queued instance with a fire time and payload.
keyFields: id: string — instance id (unique, rng/tick-salted)
defId: string — references EventDef in registry e.g. 'event.scandal.affair','event.econ.shock','event.debate','event.electionDay','event.payday'
fireOnDay: number — dayIndex when it triggers (heap key)
priority: number — tiebreak within the same day (lower fires first; e.g. economic shocks before news cycle)
kind: EventKind — 'scheduled' | 'random' | 'chained'
payload: Record<string, unknown> — def-specific data (which candidate, magnitude, which race)
sourceSeed: number — the rng seed snapshot used to GENERATE this event's effects, so re-resolution is deterministic
status: 'pending'|'fired'|'cancelled'
cancelKey: string | null — optional dedupe/cancel handle (e.g. cancel a scheduled rally if office withdrawn)
relationships: EventDef holds: trigger (scheduled cron-like OR hazard fn), guard (predicate on state), effects (list of actions to dispatch), weight, cooldownDays, oncePerGame flag, newsHeadlineTemplate
Heap ordered by (fireOnDay, priority, tickCount-of-insert, id)
Firing an event dispatches its effect actions through the same reducer — events are just a deterministic action source

coreEntities.name: Action + LoggedAction
coreEntities.purpose: The only legal way to mutate state. A discriminated union of plain-data commands handled by pure reducer functions.
keyFields: type: string — discriminant e.g. 'core/tick','core/scheduleEvent','graph/setPolicyLevel','graph/applyShock','core/setGranularity','sim/advanceTo'
payload: object — type-specific, fully serializable
meta?: { source: 'player'|'event'|'ai'|'system'; tick: number } — provenance for logging/AI
relationships: applyAction(state, action, ctx: ReducerCtx) -> GameState; ctx carries { registry, rngFork(salt) } so reducers stay pure (no global RNG)
Core reducer handles core/* and graph/* and event/*; other subsystems register reducer slices via combineReducers-style map keyed by action namespace
LoggedAction = Action & { atDay, atTick, resultingContentHash? } appended to actionLog for replay

coreEntities.name: GraphState (runtime)
coreEntities.purpose: The mutable runtime half of the effects graph stored in GameState.
keyFields: values: Record<string, number> — current value per node id
targets: Record<string, number> — last pre-inertia target per node (for debugging/derivative display)
lagBuffers: Record<string, number[]> — per-edge ring buffers of delayed source values, keyed by edge id
order: string[] — cached evaluation order (topo of the condensation of SCCs; recomputed only if content changes, not stored if derivable from registry — stored as hash check)
dirty: boolean — set when a policy/shock changes inputs, to allow skipping full eval on idle ticks (optional optimization)
relationships: Initialized from registry node baseValues at createGame
Mutated only inside the graph tick step; read by everything (voter utility calc reads sim values)

coreEntities.name: Engine (facade) + ContentRegistry
coreEntities.purpose: The public API object the UI holds, and the immutable static content it wraps. Engine is NOT serialized; it is reconstructed around a GameState.
keyFields: Engine.createGame(opts: CreateGameOpts): Engine — opts {rootSeed, mode, scenarioId, ruleset, difficulty}
Engine.dispatch(action: Action): void — validates, runs reducer, updates internal state, emits change to subscribers
Engine.tick(steps=1): TickResult — advances calendar by granularity, runs event scan + graph eval + history append; returns digest
Engine.getState(): Readonly<GameState> — frozen snapshot (Object.freeze in dev) for UI
Engine.serialize(): string / Engine.deserialize(json): Engine — JSON save/load with migration
Engine.subscribe(fn): () => void — change notification for Zustand bridge
ContentRegistry: { nodes, edges, eventDefs, actionHandlers, version, hash } — frozen, built from @data packs
relationships: UI -> engine.dispatch / engine.getState only; never touches GameState directly
engine.tick internally builds an ordered pipeline of pure step functions; each step is independently unit-tested
Registry validated at build (no dangling edge endpoints, unique ids, acyclic-after-condensation check)

mechanics: TICK PIPELINE (deterministic, ordered): engine.tick() runs steps in fixed order so results are reproducible: (1) advanceCalendar — dayIndex += daysPerTick(granularity), recompute date cache, tickCount++; (2) forkTickRng — derive ephemeral streams per system: rngTick = forkRng(rootStream, `tick:${tickCount}`); subForks for 'events','graph','ai'; (3) scanEvents — pop all queued events with fireOnDay<=dayIndex in heap order, dispatch their effect actions; (4) rollRandomEvents — for each random EventDef whose guard passes and cooldown elapsed, hazard roll p=hazardRate*daysPerTick clamped, if rng.chance(p) schedule/fire it; (5) evalGraph — relaxation update (below); (6) subsystemTicks — call registered per-tick hooks (campaign/economy/polling) in registration order; (7) appendDigest — push TickDigest to history ring; (8) bumpRngStreams — persist advanced long-lived streams back to state.
daysPerTick(granularity): day=>1, week=>7, month=>daysInCurrentMonth (so monthly ticks land on consistent calendar boundaries; governing fast-forward uses week=7 to keep weekday-of-event stable).

GRAPH RELAXATION (handles cycles + inertia): per tick, for each node compute target via incoming edges using DELAYED source values from lagBuffers; iterate RELAX_ITERS=4 fixed passes over evaluation `order` (topo order of SCC condensation; within an SCC use previous-tick values to break the cycle — Gauss-Seidel style). Formula per node: target = clamp(base + Σ_e contribution_e, min, max); contribution_e = weight_e * transfer(delayedSrc_e). After passes: value_new = inertia*value_prev + (1-inertia)*target; then if volatility>0 add rng-gaussian(0, volatility) and re-clamp. Finally push value into each outgoing edge's lagBuffer (ring of length lag+1; delayedSrc = buffer[(head-lag) mod len]).

TRANSFER FUNCTIONS: linear(w,x)=w*x; multiplier returns (1+w*x) folded multiplicatively into a node's product accumulator (for nodes flagged multiplicative); sigmoid(w,x)=w*(1/(1+exp(-curve*(x-0.5)))-0.5)*2; step(w,x)=x>=threshold? w:0; inverse(w,x)=w*(1-x). All bounded so a single edge can't exceed |w|.

RNG ALGORITHM (mulberry32): nextU32(rng){ rng.s = (rng.s + 0x6D2B79F5)>>>0; let t=rng.s; t=Math.imul(t ^ (t>>>15), t|1); t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t>>>7), t|61); return ((t ^ (t>>>14))>>>0); } nextFloat=nextU32/2^32. Seed forking via splitmix64-on-uint32: hash(salt) folds string chars (fnv1a) then mixes: z=(seed+0x9E3779B9)>>>0; z=Math.imul(z^(z>>>16),0x21f0aaad)>>>0; z=Math.imul(z^(z>>>15),0x735a2d97)>>>0; z^=z>>>15; return z>>>0.

SEED MANAGEMENT POLICY: rootSeed -> named long-lived streams created at createGame: rngStreams = { events: fork(root,'events'), graphNoise: fork(root,'graph.noise'), ai: fork(root,'ai'), polling: fork(root,'polling') }. Per-tick ephemera are re-forked from the long-lived stream salted by tickCount and NOT stored — this guarantees that adding a new subsystem that consumes RNG cannot shift another subsystem's stream (stream isolation = no 'RNG bleed' regressions in tests).

EVENT HAZARD MODEL: random events use a per-tick hazard. EventDef.baseHazardPerDay (e.g. scandal=0.0008) optionally scaled by state predicates (e.g. *2 if situation.lowApproval active). Probability for this tick = 1-(1-hazardPerDay)^daysPerTick to be granularity-invariant. cooldownDays prevents re-fire; oncePerGame tracked in flags. Scheduled events (electionDay, debate, payday) are inserted at createGame / on race-creation via firstTuesdayAfterFirstMonday and recurring schedules.

EVENT QUEUE: binary min-heap over compositeKey = fireOnDay*1e6 + priority*1e3 + (insertionTickCount mod 1e3); serialized as a flat array (heap invariant re-established on deserialize via heapify, so array order need not be canonical — but we sort on serialize for stable diffs). Cancellation marks status='cancelled' and is skipped on pop (lazy deletion) to keep heap mutation simple and deterministic.

ACTION DISPATCH: dispatch(action) => validate(action) (zod-like runtime check in dev, type-only in prod) => newState = rootReducer(state, action, ctx) => freeze in dev => set internal => notify subscribers. rootReducer routes by action.type namespace prefix to the matching reducer slice; unknown type throws in dev, no-ops with warn in prod. Reducers use structural sharing (spread only changed branches) so React memoization works and undo via state snapshots is cheap.

SAVE/LOAD + MIGRATION: serialize = JSON.stringify({ ...state, schemaVersion: SCHEMA_VERSION }). deserialize(json): parse -> read schemaVersion v -> run MIGRATIONS[v], MIGRATIONS[v+1], ... up to current, each a pure (any)=>any function with its own test fixtures -> validate shape -> verify contentHash matches active registry (warn-and-continue if minor, refuse if major) -> heapify event queue. Migrations are append-only and never edited once shipped.

DETERMINISM GUARANTEES: no Date.now/Math.random/Object key iteration order dependence in sim paths (always sort keys when order matters). createGame(seed) + same action sequence + same registry hash => identical serialize() output. This is the property tested by the replay invariant test.

HISTORY DIGEST: each tick appends TickDigest { dayIndex, tickCount, simSnapshot: Pick of key sim values, firedEventIds: string[], rngCursorHash } — small, used for trend charts and to assert replay equivalence cheaply via rngCursorHash chain.
