tddNotes: RNG determinism: createRng(12345); calling nextU32 N times then re-creating createRng(12345) and calling N times yields identical sequence (golden array of first 10 uint32s asserted against a frozen literal).

RNG stream isolation: forkRng(root,'events') and forkRng(root,'ai') produce different sequences; draining one stream by 1000 calls does NOT change the other's next value (assert exact value before and after).
RNG distribution sanity: 100k nextFloat() samples have mean in [0.49,0.51] and all values in [0,1).

Calendar conversion roundtrip: for dayIndex in a sweep (0..40000), dateToDayIndex(dayIndexToDate(d))===d; and 2026-11-03 is the first-Tuesday-after-first-Monday => isElectionDay true, 2026-11-02 false.
Granularity advance: tick on 'week' advances dayIndex by exactly 7 and preserves weekday; 'month' on Jan 15 lands keeping month-boundary logic (daysInMonth correct for Feb leap years 2024 vs 2025).
Event queue ordering: inserting events out of order (day 10 pri 2, day 5 pri 1, day 5 pri 0, day 10 pri 1) and popping all <= day 10 yields exact order [d5p0,d5p1,d10p1,d10p2].
Event cancellation: scheduleEvent then cancelEvent(cancelKey) => event never appears in a subsequent tick's firedEventIds.

Hazard granularity invariance: a random event with baseHazardPerDay=0.01 fires with statistically equal expected count whether advancing 70 single-day ticks or 10 week-ticks (assert fired-count within tolerance over fixed seed, AND assert exact equality of the per-tick probability formula 1-(1-p)^days).
Graph equilibrium: with no policy inputs and zero volatility, every node converges to its baseValue within EPS=1e-4 after enough ticks (homeostasis test).
Graph inertia: a node with inertia=0.9 reaches <63% of a step change only after ~ the expected number of ticks (assert monotonic approach and that inertia=0 jumps immediately to target).
Graph lag: an edge with lag=3 means a step change in source first affects target's target-value exactly 3 ticks later, not before (assert target unchanged for ticks t..t+2, changed at t+3).
Graph cycle stability: a 2-node positive feedback loop (economy<->confidence, weights chosen) does NOT diverge — values stay within [min,max] over 1000 ticks (no NaN/Infinity, bounded).
Clamping: applying a large graph/applyShock cannot push any node outside [min,max].

Reducer purity: applyAction(state, action, ctx) returns a NEW object and does not mutate the input (deep-freeze input, assert no throw); unrelated state branches are referentially identical (structural sharing).

Replay invariant (the headline test): createGame(seed=777) + a recorded action+tick sequence => serialize() equals a second independent run of the same sequence, byte-for-byte; also equals deserialize(serialize(...)) then continue => same final hash.
Save/load roundtrip: deserialize(serialize(state)) deep-equals state (after re-heapify), including rngStreams cursors so the next tick is identical.
Migration: a v1 fixture JSON run through deserialize upgrades schemaVersion to current and passes shape validation; each MIGRATIONS[n] has a focused fixture asserting the single field it changes.

Content validation: a registry with a dangling edge endpoint or duplicate node id fails buildRegistry() with a precise error; a registry whose condensation has a cycle through a 'policy' input node is rejected.
contentHash guard: deserialize of a save with mismatched contentHash for a MAJOR registry change throws; minor change warns and proceeds.

Engine facade: engine.getState() returns a frozen object (mutating it throws in dev); dispatch notifies subscribers exactly once per action; tick(3) is equivalent to tick(1) three times (assert equal final state).
risks: Floating-point reproducibility across platforms: relaxation/sigmoid use Math.exp which can differ in last ULP between engines; mitigate by hashing rounded values (toFixed/quantize to 1e-6) for replay-equivalence checks rather than raw bit equality, and keep all sim math in plain JS doubles (no WASM/SIMD).

SCC/cycle handling in the graph can oscillate or converge slowly if weights are tuned badly; RELAX_ITERS is fixed at 4 so a poorly-authored content pack could produce non-equilibrium — needs a content-lint test and a per-SCC damping factor knob.
Event-queue lazy deletion (cancelled events left in heap) could grow unbounded in very long games; add periodic compaction every N ticks and cap on serialize.

Determinism is fragile against any accidental use of Object key iteration order, Date, Math.random, or Set/Map serialization order — needs an ESLint rule banning Math.random/Date.now in src/engine and a CI replay test as a tripwire.

Action-log growth: storing every action for replay bloats saves; make actionLog opt-in/sampled and keep the authoritative replay path = rootSeed + content + scripted scenario, with actionLog as a debug aid only.
schemaVersion migration chain must stay append-only; an edited historical migration silently corrupts old saves — enforce with a migrations snapshot/lock test.

Mode-switch mid-game (campaign->governing) changes tick granularity and which subsystems advance; ensure pending day-scheduled events still fire correctly when ticking by week (scan is <= dayIndex so safe, but partial-week event timing loses day precision in governing mode — document as intended).

designs.overview:
The front-end is a pure render of engine state plus an action-dispatch channel. Hard rule: the React tree never mutates engine state and never reaches into engine internals; it reads an immutable `GameState` snapshot and dispatches serializable `PlayerAction` objects. This mirrors the existing repo layout (`@engine`, `@data`, `@ui` aliases; engine tests run in `node`, UI tests opt into `jsdom` via `// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

STATE MANAGEMENT — recommendation: Zustand (already a dep), NOT reducer+context. Rationale: (1) the engine already owns the reducer (a pure `applyAction(state, action, ctx) => GameState` and `tick(state) => GameState`), so React's job is only to hold the current snapshot and re-render selectively; (2) Zustand gives selector-level subscriptions (`useStore(s => s.slice)`) which avoid the whole-tree re-render that `useContext` causes on every tick — critical because a tick can touch thousands of voter/precinct values; (3) Zustand stores live outside React, so non-React code (autosave, web worker bridge) can read/write without hooks. Context is reserved only for static, rarely-changing things (theme, i18n, feature flags, the dispatch fn itself).

THE BRIDGE (engine<->UI decoupling). One module `@ui/store/gameStore.ts` creates a Zustand store whose ONLY engine-typed field is `state: GameState` plus derived UI-only fields (selectedOfficeId, openPanels, mapViewport, etc.). The engine is never imported into components; only the store and a set of pure `selectors/*.ts` import engine types. Components import selectors + a `useDispatch()` hook. Flow: component calls `dispatch({type:'BUY_AD', ...})` -> store's `dispatch` validates via engine's `validateAction(state, action)` (returns `ActionResult{ok,errors,cost}`), if ok runs `applyAction` to produce a new immutable snapshot, calls `set({state:next})`, and pushes the action onto an `actionLog` for replay/determinism testing. Time advance (`END_TURN`/`tick`) runs the SAME path. For long ticks, the engine call is wrapped behind an async `EngineClient` interface with two impls: `InlineEngineClient` (calls synchronously, used in tests + small saves) and `WorkerEngineClient` (Comlink-wrapped Web Worker, used in prod so a heavy national tick never blocks the main thread). UI subscribes to a `tickStatus: 'idle'|'running'` flag to show a simulating overlay.

DERIVED/MEMO LAYER. Expensive read-side aggregations (national popular-vote projection, demographic crosstabs, the Democracy-graph layout) are computed by pure selector functions memoized with `proxy-memoize` or a hand-rolled `weakMemoByState` keyed on `state.meta.revision` (a monotonically incrementing integer the engine bumps each applyAction). Components never recompute these inline.

RENDERING STACK / LIBRARIES (all MIT/permissive, tree-shakeable, web-first):
 - Routing: none heavy — a tiny enum-driven `<ScreenRouter>` switching on `ui.screen` (no react-router needed; the game is a state machine, not URL-driven, though we keep `?screen=` sync for deep links/debug).
 - Charts (polling, approval, fundraising, time series, crosstab bars): Visx (@visx/* — D3 scales as React primitives, fully composable, SSR-safe, themeable) as primary; Recharts as a faster-to-ship fallback for simple line/bar in the first slice. Avoid Chart.js (canvas, harder to test/theme).
 - Maps (US states, congressional districts, counties, precincts choropleth): MapLibre GL JS (open-source, vector tiles, GPU choropleth at precinct scale) for the production map; D3-geo + topojson-client (us-atlas) for the first slice (lighter, deterministic, easy to snapshot-test as SVG). Geometry served as TopoJSON, joined to engine geoIds.
 - The signature Democracy graph: a custom force/DAG renderer on React-Flow (@xyflow/react) for node interactivity (drag, zoom, edge hover, pan), with edge curvature + animated flow particles to show causal effect sign/strength. For pure auto-layout we precompute positions with d3-force offline-ish (in a worker) and feed React-Flow controlled node positions. Fallback/first-slice: a static SVG graph using elkjs layout.
 - Virtualization (long lists: every US office, donor lists, voter-group tables): @tanstack/react-virtual.
 - Animation/transitions (vote tallies ticking up on election night, number rolls): Framer Motion (motion/react) + a `useCountUp` hook.
 - Styling: CSS Modules + CSS custom properties for theming (already a global.css). No Tailwind required, but acceptable; keep tokens in `:root`. Dark mode via `data-theme`.
 - Forms (candidate creation, bill drafting): react-hook-form + Zod resolver (Zod schemas double as engine input validation — share the schema between UI and engine boundary).

SCREEN/FLOW MAP (driven by `ui.screen: ScreenId` enum). MainMenu -> NewGameSetup -> CandidateCreator -> ElectionBrowser (filter/search ANY US office) -> CampaignDashboard (sub-tabs: HQ/Tycoon, Map, Calendar, Actions, Fundraising, Polling, Opposition) -> ElectionNight -> (if won) GoverningDashboard (sub-tabs: Legislature, BillEditor, FloorVotes, Approval, Constituents). A persistent `<TopBar>` (cash, date, approval, next-election countdown, save) and `<EventFeed>` (ticker of sim events) frame all in-game screens. `<TurnControls>` (Advance Day/Week, with confirmation when actions remain) is global.

COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE: feature-folder layout under `src/ui/`: `app/` (shell, router, providers), `store/` (gameStore, dispatch, engineClient), `selectors/` (pure, engine-aware, the ONLY UI code that imports engine types beyond the store), `screens/<Screen>/`, `components/` (dumb, presentational, engine-agnostic — take plain props), `viz/` (charts, map, causal graph), `hooks/`, `theme/`. Strict dependency rule enforced by ESLint `no-restricted-imports`: `components/**` and `viz/**` may NOT import from `@engine` or `@data` — they receive view-model props only. This keeps presentational pieces unit-testable with zero engine setup.

TESTING STRATEGY (two tiers, matching repo's node/jsdom split): (1) Engine = pure Vitest in `node` env, deterministic seeded RNG, the bulk of correctness coverage; coverage config already limits to `src/engine/**` + `src/data/**`. (2) UI: selectors get pure unit tests in `node` (no DOM) since they're just functions of state — cheap and high-value. Components/screens get @testing-library/react tests with `// @vitest-environment jsdom`, rendered against a fabricated `GameState` fixture + a mock `EngineClient` (so dispatch is asserted, not the engine re-run). Interaction tests use @testing-library/user-event. Viz gets SVG snapshot tests for the d3/visx output (stable because engine is deterministic). A small set of action-roundtrip tests assert that clicking a button dispatches the exact expected `PlayerAction`. Accessibility regression via jest-axe on each screen.

ACCESSIBILITY: semantic landmarks (`<main> <nav> <aside>`), all interactive viz nodes are real `<button>`/`role` elements with keyboard handlers, the causal graph has a parallel accessible data-table view toggle, charts ship an `aria-label` summary + offscreen data table, focus management on screen transitions (move focus to `<h1>`), `prefers-reduced-motion` disables count-up/particle animations, WCAG AA contrast tokens, color is never the sole encoding (vote/party also uses pattern/label).

FIRST VERTICAL SLICE (production-quality, narrow): one race — a single US House district special election. MainMenu -> CandidateCreator (name, party, 6 issue sliders) -> skip browser (pre-selected district) -> CampaignDashboard with only 3 working tabs: Actions (Buy Ad, Hold Rally, Fundraise — each a real dispatch with cost/cooldown), Polling (one Visx line chart of your share vs opponent over weeks, fed by engine), Calendar/TurnControls (Advance Week). -> ElectionNight (animated tally + win/lose). Everything else stubbed behind feature flags. This exercises the entire spine: store, dispatch, engineClient (inline), one selector chain, one chart, one screen-transition, deterministic test — proving the architecture end-to-end before breadth is added.

coreEntities.name: GameStore (Zustand store shape)
coreEntities.purpose: Single source of truth for React. Wraps the engine snapshot + UI state + the dispatch/tick actions. The only module allowed to call the EngineClient.
keyFields: state: GameState — immutable engine snapshot (revision-stamped)
ui: UiState — UI-only state
actionLog: PlayerAction[] — ordered, serializable, for replay/determinism tests
lastResult: ActionResult | null — outcome (cost paid, errors) of most recent dispatch for UI feedback

advanceTurn: (unit: 'day'|'week') => Promise<TickReport> — runs engine tick(s) via EngineClient

coreEntities.name: PlayerAction (discriminated union)
coreEntities.purpose: The ONLY way the UI mutates the simulation. Plain serializable objects; each has a Zod schema shared with the engine boundary for validation.

payload — per-type (see dataTaxonomy)

coreEntities.purpose: Engine's verdict on an action, surfaced to UI for affordances (disable buttons, show cost, explain why blocked).

errors: ActionError[] — { code: ActionErrorCode, message: string, field?: string }
cost: { cash?: number, actionPoints?: number, politicalCapital?: number, staffHours?: number }
previewDelta?: Record<string, number> — projected effect for tooltips (e.g. +0.4 name recognition)

coreEntities.name: ViewModel objects (selector outputs)
coreEntities.purpose: Plain, engine-agnostic shapes produced by selectors and passed to presentational components, so components/viz never import engine types.

MapVM: { features: { geoId:string, value:number, leaderParty:PartyId|null, label:string }[], metric: ChoroplethMetric, domain:[number,number], colorStops:[number,string][] }
CausalGraphVM: { nodes: GraphNodeVM[], edges: GraphEdgeVM[] }

coreEntities.name: EngineClient (interface)
coreEntities.purpose: Abstraction over where the engine runs, so heavy national ticks can move off the main thread without changing call sites or tests.
keyFields: validate(state: GameState, action: PlayerAction): ActionResult
apply(state: GameState, action: PlayerAction): { state: GameState, result: ActionResult }
tick(state: GameState, unit:'day'|'week'): { state: GameState, report: TickReport }

coreEntities.name: ScreenRouter / ScreenId
coreEntities.purpose: State-machine navigation. UI is driven by an enum, not URLs, but mirrored to ?screen= for deep-link/debug.
keyFields: ScreenId: 'mainMenu'|'newGame'|'candidateCreator'|'electionBrowser'|'campaign'|'electionNight'|'governing'|'settings'|'load'
allowedTransitions: Record<ScreenId, ScreenId[]> — guards illegal nav
onEnter(screen): focus <h1>, fire analytics, lazy-load chunk

mechanics: Selector subscription: components call useStore(selectPollVM) where selectPollVM is wrapped in weakMemoByState — it caches on state.meta.revision so re-running the same revision returns the identical reference, letting React.memo'd children skip re-render. Formula: cacheKey = `${selectorId}:${state.meta.revision}:${JSON.stringify(args)}`.

Dispatch pipeline: dispatch(action) => result = engineClient.validate(state, action); if(!result.ok){ set(s=>({lastResult:result, ui:{...s.ui, toasts:[...toasts, errToast]}})); return result } else { const {state:next,result} = engineClient.apply(state, action); set({state:next, lastResult:result, actionLog:[...log, {...action, issuedOnTick: state.calendar.tick}]}); return result }. Determinism invariant: replaying actionLog from the seeded initial state reproduces state byte-for-byte.

Turn advance with worker: advanceTurn('week') => set ui.tickStatus='running'; const {state:next,report} = await engineClient.tick(state,'week'); set({state:next, ui:{tickStatus:'idle'}}); enqueue toasts from report.events. Main thread stays responsive; a <SimulatingOverlay/> shows a progress spinner driven by worker postMessage progress (0..1).

Button affordance: each action button computes disabled/cost by calling engineClient.validate(state, candidateAction) memoized per revision — shows cost chips (cash, AP) and a tooltip listing previewDelta and any blocking errors, so the player sees consequences before committing (Democracy-style feedforward).

Causal graph layout: nodes = issues+policies+voterGroups+situations from selectCausalGraphVM. Edge stroke width = |effect.weight| mapped via scaleLinear([0,maxWeight],[1,6]) px; edge color = sign (green +, red -); animated dash offset speed ∝ |weight| and only when reducedMotion=false. Node fill = current value via diverging color scale scaleDiverging([-1,0,1], interpolateRdYlGn). Layout positions precomputed by d3-force in a worker, then handed to React-Flow as controlled nodes so dragging is user-overridable but stable across ticks.

Map choropleth: MapVM.value per geoId chosen by ChoroplethMetric; color via d3 scaleSequential or scaleDiverging on domain. For two-party leader maps, fill = leaderParty color with opacity = margin/0.3 clamped to [0.15,1] so blowouts saturate and tossups fade — matches familiar US election cartography. Precinct level only renders when zoom>=8 (MapLibre) to bound DOM/GPU cost.

Polling chart: PollVM points are the engine's modeled support with margin of error; render Visx LinePath per candidate plus a translucent AreaPath band [share-moe, share+moe]. X axis = game weeks to election; a vertical now-line marks current tick. Hover crosshair reads nearest tick via bisector.

Election-night tally: useCountUp animates displayed votes from prevReported to reported over 800ms easeOutCubic, but instantly snaps if reducedMotion. Called-race logic is engine-provided (race.called, race.winnerId); UI only renders the call banner + confetti (suppressed under reducedMotion).

Form->action bridge: CandidateCreator uses react-hook-form with a Zod schema candidateSchema; onSubmit maps form values to a CREATE_CANDIDATE action. The SAME candidateSchema is imported by the engine boundary to re-validate, so client and engine cannot diverge.

Optimistic vs authoritative: dispatch is synchronous for inline client (no optimism needed). For worker client, cheap actions still validate synchronously (validate runs on a cached lightweight state proxy) but apply awaits; UI disables the control and shows a pending spinner until resolve to keep state authoritative (no rollback complexity).

Lazy code-splitting: each screen is React.lazy(()=>import('./screens/...')); the CampaignDashboard viz (map, graph) split further so the first slice bundle excludes MapLibre/React-Flow until needed. Suspense fallback = skeleton.

Autosave: a store.subscribe on state.meta.revision debounced 2s serializes exportSave() to IndexedDB (idb-keyval); manual Save writes a named slot. Save schema is versioned (save.schemaVersion) with a migrations map applied on load.

tddNotes: selectPollVM: given a GameState fixture with two candidates and 4 recorded poll ticks, returns 2 series each with 4 points, shares in [0,1], and asOfDate equal to calendar.date — pure node test, no DOM.

weakMemoByState invariant: calling a memoized selector twice with the same state (same meta.revision) returns the IDENTICAL reference (===); after a dispatch that bumps revision, it returns a fresh reference.

dispatch happy path: with a mock EngineClient returning {ok:true, cost:{cash:5000}}, dispatching BUY_AD appends exactly one entry to actionLog, sets lastResult.ok=true, and calls engineClient.apply exactly once.

dispatch blocked path: mock validate returns {ok:false, errors:[{code:'INSUFFICIENT_CASH'}]}; dispatch does NOT call apply, does NOT mutate actionLog, pushes one error toast, and returns the failing result.

determinism roundtrip: starting from seeded initial state, applying actionLog of 20 actions via InlineEngineClient yields a state whose JSON.stringify equals a recorded golden snapshot (guards engine/UI contract).

Action button affordance (jsdom): rendering <ActionButton action=BUY_AD> against a state with cash<spend shows the button disabled and a cost chip; with sufficient cash it is enabled — assert via getByRole('button',{disabled}).

CandidateCreator (jsdom): filling required fields and submitting dispatches exactly one CREATE_CANDIDATE action whose payload matches the form (assert on the mock dispatch); submitting with empty name shows a field error and dispatches nothing.
ScreenRouter guard: attempting an illegal transition (mainMenu -> governing) is a no-op and logs; legal transition updates ui.screen and moves focus to the new <h1> (assert document.activeElement).
UsMap selector (node): selectMapVM with metric='twoPartyLeader' returns features whose leaderParty matches the higher-share candidate's party and value within domain; unknown geoId is omitted.
CausalGraph SVG snapshot: selectCausalGraphVM over a fixed 5-node/6-edge fixture produces a stable VM (node ids, edge signs, weights) — snapshot test; edge weight->stroke mapping is monotonic.

Accessibility (jest-axe): each screen fixture (MainMenu, CandidateCreator, CampaignDashboard, ElectionNight) renders with zero axe violations; CausalGraph exposes a toggle that reveals a <table> equivalent.
reduced-motion: with ui.reducedMotion=true, useCountUp returns the final value immediately (no interpolation frames) and confetti component renders null.
ElectionNight: given a race with called=true and winnerId=player, the call banner renders the player's name and the win state; with called=false it renders 'Polls open'/'Counting'.
risks: Worker boundary cost: moving ticks to a Web Worker means GameState crosses structured-clone on every tick. If state is large (national precinct data), clone cost may dominate. Mitigation: keep WorkerEngineClient optional behind ff.worker, use transferable/SharedArrayBuffer for hot numeric arrays, or keep the authoritative state in the worker and ship only diffs + the visible slice to the main thread.

Selector recomputation: if engine bumps meta.revision on every micro-mutation, memoization keys churn and expensive selectors (graph layout, national crosstabs) recompute too often. Mitigation: coarse revision bumps per applyAction/tick only, plus per-selector dependency narrowing (subscribe to substate slices, not whole state).
React-Flow + MapLibre bundle weight: both are heavy. Mitigation: aggressive React.lazy code-splitting and the d3/SVG fallbacks for the first slice keep initial load small; only load on tab entry.

Shared Zod schemas: if engine and UI import the same schema but the engine must stay DOM/IO-free, ensure schemas live in @data (neutral) not @ui. Risk of accidental engine->ui import; enforce with ESLint no-restricted-imports boundary rule.

Determinism vs animation: UI animations must never feed back into engine state (e.g. count-up must read engine totals, not drive them). Risk of nondeterminism if a component dispatches on a timer; forbid timer-driven dispatch outside TurnControls.

Save schema drift: UI-only UiState must not be serialized into the canonical save, or loads from older engine versions break. Keep separate persistence channels (save = engine state; prefs = UiState).

moduleLayout.responsibility: The deterministic spine. Owns GameState root, Calendar (dayIndex clock), RngState + pure rng helpers, the EventQueue (binary min-heap), the Democracy-style effects graph (SimNode/SimEdge runtime + relaxation), the global ScheduledEffect ledger, the root reducer applyAction/tickReducer, serialize/deserialize + migration chain, and the ContentRegistry contract. Imports NOTHING from other subsystems; everyone imports it.

mulberry32 + splitmix64 fork. Serializable RngState struct + pure functions (nextU32, nextFloat, nextRange, nextInt, chance, pick, shuffle, forkRng). Plus a thin stateless Rng wrapper used at call sites that threads RngState. NO Math.random, NO Date.

dayIndex<->date conversion (proleptic Gregorian, epoch 2000-01-01), addDays, weekday, daysInMonth, firstTuesdayAfterFirstMonday(year), isElectionDay, tickGranularity->daysPerTick. No JS Date at runtime.

Effects-graph runtime: GraphState (values/targets/lagBuffers), SCC-condensation topo order, RELAX_ITERS relaxation pass with inertia + lag ring buffers + transfer functions + seeded gaussian noise. Pure evalGraph(state,ctx).

EventDef/GameEvent, binary-heap EventQueue (serialized as array, heapify on load), scheduleEvent/cancelEvent (lazy deletion), scanDueEvents, hazard-roll model for random events (granularity-invariant 1-(1-p)^days).

The global ScheduledEffect ledger: pushEffect, appliedMagnitudeAt (ramp/decay/sunset math), and the read API the electorate/economy consume. Both campaign and governing lower their domain effects into this single ledger.

Root applyAction(state,action,ctx)->state with structural sharing, namespace-routed reducer slices (core/, graph/, campaign/, gov/, election/), tickReducer (the fixed tick pipeline), revision bump. Pure; ctx carries {registry, rngFork}.
serialize/deserialize, schemaVersion + append-only MIGRATIONS chain, contentHash guard, event-queue re-heapify on load.
Shared core types: GameState, Calendar, GraphState, EventQueueState, Action, ReducerCtx, branded id types (EntityId, DayIndex, Seed), TickResult/TickDigest, EntityStores container contract.

Electoral structure: jurisdictions tree, OfficeDefinition, ElectoralSystemDef, TermRule, materializeSeats, Seat/Officeholder, ElectionInstance/Candidacy, the SeatAllocator strategies (FPTP/runoff/RCV/STV/EC), scheduler (nextElectionsOnOrAfter). Mostly pure data + pure allocator functions.

Pure (votesByCandidate, systemDef, rng) => AllocationResult dispatch on AllocationMethod. FPTP, two-round, IRV, STV (Droop/Gregory), block, party-list, electoral-college, retention. Deterministic tie-breaks.
Pure arithmetic over TermRule + cohort to compute nextElectionYear/Date per seat; emits scheduled ElectionInstances + electionDay GameEvents into core.

Voter simulation: IssueDef/DemographicAxis/PartyDef registries, GroupState (weighted overlapping segments), ElectorateState per jurisdiction, evaluateElectorate (deterministic utility+softmax+turnout), runOpinionTick (inertia/events), conductPoll (sampled/noisy). Consumes core ledger sim values; exposes ElectorateReadModel.
Pure, RNG-free spatial proximity + valence + party loyalty + identity + incumbency utility, multinomial-logit vote share, logistic turnout, group contribution aggregation.
conductPoll: Dirichlet sampling, MoE, house effects, likely-voter screens. Only this + runOpinionTick take an rng.

Campaign engine: CandidateState/PlatformStance, CampaignState (finances/org/strategy), data-driven CampaignActionDef + EffectSpec, applyCampaignAction & tickCampaign reducers, the multiplier-chain effect pipeline that LOWERS EffectSpecs into core ScheduledEffects tagged as ElectorateEffects. Integer-cents money.
The effect pipeline: magnitude = base*staffMult*officeMult*strategyMult*DR*fatigue*rngJitter, reach scaling by segment sizes from ElectorateReadModel, emit ElectorateEffect (a typed ScheduledEffect).
FinanceState ledger (append-only, integer cents), donor pools, FEC limit enforcement, burn-rate/projection selectors.

Legislation engine: Bill/Provision/EffectOp/FiscalNote, data-driven LegislativeProcess state machine, Legislator whip-utility model, Committee/ExecutiveOffice/Agency/Deal, advanceLegislation reducer. Lowers enacted EffectOps into the core ledger.

Generic interpreter walking a LegislativeProcess (stages/gates/transitions): votes, thresholds, filibuster/cloture, committee markup, veto/override, amendments-as-data re-deriving ideology+fiscalNote.
Pure legislator vote-utility, logistic p_yea, whip count, deal/logroll matching. Reads denormalized DistrictProfile snapshots only.

The Engine facade: createGame/dispatch/tick/getState/serialize/deserialize/subscribe. Reconstructed around a GameState; never serialized; holds the ContentRegistry. The ONLY thing the store imports beyond selectors+types.

Content packs (neutral, no engine logic, no React): issues.json, demographics.json, parties.json, media.json, electoralRuleset (offices/systems/termRules/jurisdictions), campaign/ (actionDefs, staffRoles, officeTiers, adChannels), governing/ (processes, committees, effectOp templates), starterScenario. Loaded into ContentRegistry at createGame. Also home of SHARED Zod schemas (so engine stays DOM/IO-free and UI can reuse them).
Zod schemas shared by engine boundary (validateAction) and UI forms (react-hook-form resolver). Neutral location so neither @engine nor @ui owns them.

gameStore.ts (Zustand: {state:GameState, ui:UiState, actionLog, dispatch, advanceTurn}), engineClient.ts (InlineEngineClient default + WorkerEngineClient behind flag). The ONLY UI module allowed to call the Engine facade.

Pure engine-aware selectors producing engine-agnostic ViewModels (PollVM, MapVM, OfficeRowVM, HqVM, CausalGraphVM). Memoized by state.meta.revision. The only UI code besides the store that imports engine types.
Screen components (MainMenu, CandidateCreator, ElectionBrowser, CampaignDashboard, ElectionNight, GoverningDashboard), lazy-loaded, driven by ui.screen enum router.
Dumb presentational components taking plain props. ESLint-forbidden from importing @engine/@data (view-model props only).
Charts/map/causal-graph (Visx, d3-geo fallback, React-Flow). Also forbidden from importing @engine/@data; consume ViewModels.
App shell, ScreenRouter, providers (theme/i18n/dispatch context), TopBar/EventFeed/TurnControls frame.

foundationalTypes.name: Branded ids & primitives
foundationalTypes.tsDefinition:
// src/engine/core/types.ts
export type Brand<T, B extends string> = T & { readonly __brand: B };
export type EntityId = Brand<string, 'EntityId'>;   // candidates, seats, legislators, groups...
export type DayIndex = Brand<number, 'DayIndex'>;   // integer days since EPOCH 2000-01-01
export type Seed = Brand<number, 'Seed'>;           // uint32
export type Cents = Brand<number, 'Cents'>;          // all money is integer cents
export type Unit01 = number;  // documented [0,1]
export type Signed1 = number; // documented [-1,1]
export type ISODate = string; // 'YYYY-MM-DD', derived from DayIndex; never a JS Date
foundationalTypes.notes: Brands cost nothing at runtime, are JSON-transparent, and stop the classic seatId/personId/groupId mixups across the six subsystems. Cents brand enforces the campaign-engine no-float-money rule at the type level.

foundationalTypes.name: RngState (serializable) + Rng wrapper
foundationalTypes.notes: Reconciles Core's serializable RngState with Campaign's SeededRng and Governing's Rng-with-fork. The struct + pure functions are the source of truth; Rng is a thin cursor wrapper used at call sites. Every stochastic decision uses rng.fork(deterministic salt like `${billId}:${legId}:${tick}` or `tick:${tickCount}`) so adding a subsystem can never shift another's stream (no RNG bleed).

foundationalTypes.name: Calendar
foundationalTypes.notes: Single canonical clock. Campaign's daysElapsed and Governing's tick all map onto Calendar.dayIndex / tickCount. Subsystems store absolute DayIndex values (electionDay, resolveDay, enactedTick) never relative offsets.

foundationalTypes.name: GameState root + EntityStores
foundationalTypes.notes: Core owns the root and the container contract; each subsystem owns its slice and never reaches into another's. revision is bumped once per applyAction/tick (coarse) so UI selector memoization stays cheap. ledger is the single bridge — resolves the Campaign(ElectorateEffect) vs Governing(EffectOp/ScheduledEffect) duplication.

foundationalTypes.name: Effects-graph SimNode/SimEdge + GraphState
foundationalTypes.notes: SimNode/SimEdge definitions live in the immutable ContentRegistry; only values/targets/lagBuffers are in GameState. Cycles handled by relaxation (RELAX_ITERS=4, Gauss-Seidel over SCC condensation), not strict topo. This is the Democracy-4 signature mechanic and the substrate the electorate reads sim values from.

foundationalTypes.name: ScheduledEffect — the unified bridge
foundationalTypes.notes: THE key reconciliation. Campaign's ElectorateEffect and Governing's EffectOp were two names for the same thing. Both lower into this single typed ScheduledEffect with the same ramp/decay/sunset lag math. The 'electorate' target variant carries Campaign's segment reach; other variants carry Governing's policy deltas. Electorate/economy subsystems are pure CONSUMERS of this ledger — they never get written to directly.

foundationalTypes.name: Action + ReducerCtx (the only mutation channel)
foundationalTypes.notes: Unifies Core's Action, Campaign's CampaignCommand, Governing's GovAction, and UI's PlayerAction into one namespaced discriminated union routed by type prefix (core/, graph/, campaign/, gov/, election/). ReducerCtx.rngFork keeps reducers pure (no global RNG). validate/apply are the two halves the UI EngineClient calls.

foundationalTypes.name: Electorate evaluation contract
foundationalTypes.notes: evaluateElectorate is deterministic and RNG-free (only conductPoll/runOpinionTick take rng) — this is the contract that makes election night and whip counts replayable. ElectorateReadModel is the firewall: campaign reads segment sizes/lean to scale reach but writes only via emitted ScheduledEffects. AllocationResult.status carries the EC contingent-election / runoff flags rather than silently inventing a winner.

phase1BuildOrder.description: Core RNG: serializable RngState + pure helpers + forkRng. Golden-array test (createRng(12345) first 10 u32s frozen), stream-isolation test (draining 'events' fork doesn't move 'ai'), distribution sanity. This is the determinism bedrock; nothing else is trustworthy without it.
Calendar: dayIndex<->date roundtrip over a sweep, daysInMonth (leap years), firstTuesdayAfterFirstMonday (assert 2026-11-03 true, 2026-11-02 false), daysPerTick. Pure, no Date.

Core types + minimal GameState factory + EventQueue heap (insert out of order, pop in (day,priority,insert) order; cancel = lazy-skip) + ScheduledEffect ledger with appliedMagnitudeAt ramp/decay/sunset math (assert the lag fixture: 0,0,2.5,5,...,10,~5). No graph yet.

Root reducer skeleton: applyAction with namespace routing, structural sharing (assert input not mutated, unrelated branches ===), revision bump, and tickReducer running the fixed pipeline (advanceCalendar->forkTickRng->scanEvents->[graph stub]->appendDigest). Test: tick(3)===tick(1)x3.

Effects graph: GraphState init from a tiny 3-node fixture pack, relaxation with inertia + lag + transfer fns. Tests: homeostasis to baseValue (no inputs), inertia=0 jumps/0.9 lags, lag=3 delays exactly 3 ticks, 2-node positive loop stays bounded over 1000 ticks (no NaN). Wire evalGraph into tickReducer.

Electoral minimal slice: types + materializeSeats for ONE US House special-election seat from a starter ruleset, plus the FPTP allocator. Tests: FPTP {A:100,B:60,C:40}=>A margin 0.2; seeded tie-break deterministic; AllocationResult shape. (Full apportionment/Senate-classes/RCV/STV/EC deferred to phase 2.)

Electorate minimal slice: GroupState/ElectorateState + 6-issue registry, generate ~20 groups for the one district (weights sum to 1), evaluateElectorate (RNG-free utility+softmax+turnout). Tests: weights invariant, softmax sums to 1, monotonic proximity, name-rec gate (0 awareness => ~0 share), determinism (twice => deep-equal).

Polling: conductPoll (Dirichlet sample, MoE, house effect) taking a forked rng. Tests: over 10k seeded polls mean reported share within 3*SE of latent; ~95% CI coverage; LV vs Adults divergence; determinism per seed.

Campaign minimal slice: CandidateState + CampaignState + 3 CampaignActionDefs (Buy Ad, Hold Rally, Fundraise) as DATA, FinanceState integer-cents ledger, applyCampaignAction + tickCampaign, and the pipeline lowering EffectSpec->ScheduledEffect(electorate target). Tests: ledger integrity (cash===income-expense), name-rec logistic saturation toward 1, DR monotonicity, AP/stamina gating returns error without mutating, serialization roundtrip, data-driven genericity (add synthetic def, reducer handles it).

Wire the spine: ContentRegistry buildRegistry (validate no dangling edges/dup ids), Engine facade (createGame/dispatch/tick/getState/serialize/deserialize/subscribe), and the END-TO-END determinism test: createGame(seed) -> CREATE_CANDIDATE -> SELECT_ELECTION -> [BUY_AD, HOLD_RALLY, FUNDRAISE] -> advance weeks -> poll updates -> election day fires -> AllocationResult. Assert serialize() byte-identical across two runs and after a serialize/deserialize/continue.

UI store + EngineClient: gameStore (Zustand {state,ui,actionLog,dispatch,advanceTurn}), InlineEngineClient, dispatch pipeline (validate->apply->set->log). Pure node tests for selectors (selectPollVM shape, weakMemoByState identity by revision) + dispatch happy/blocked path with a mock EngineClient.

UI screens for the slice (jsdom pragma): CandidateCreator (react-hook-form + shared Zod schema, dispatches exactly one CREATE_CANDIDATE), CampaignDashboard with Actions/Polling(Visx or Recharts line)/TurnControls tabs, ElectionNight (animated tally, win/lose). Tests: action-roundtrip (button click => exact PlayerAction), affordance (disabled when cash<spend), jest-axe zero violations, reduced-motion snaps count-up.

blueprint.verticalSlice: One US House district SPECIAL election, single human candidate vs one scripted AI opponent, played end-to-end through the real engine spine. Flow: MainMenu -> CandidateCreator (name, party, 6 issue sliders -> CREATE_CANDIDATE) -> pre-selected district (SELECT_ELECTION, skipping the browser) -> CampaignDashboard with exactly three working tabs — Actions (Buy Ad / Hold Rally / Fundraise, each a real namespaced action with integer-cents cost, cooldown, AP/stamina gate, and a previewDelta), Polling (one line chart of your modeled share vs opponent over weeks fed by conductPoll), and Calendar/TurnControls (Advance Week) — then ElectionNight (animated tally + win/lose banner). Under the hood this exercises EVERY load-bearing seam exactly once: createGame+seeded RngState, the Calendar/dayIndex clock, the EventQueue firing a scheduled electionDay GameEvent, the namespaced applyAction reducer with structural sharing, the campaign effect pipeline LOWERING EffectSpecs into the single core ScheduledEffect ledger, the electorate consuming that ledger and producing both a noisy Poll (UI) and a deterministic AllocationResult (election night via the FPTP allocator), serialize/deserialize roundtrip, and the Zustand store -> InlineEngineClient -> selector -> chart UI path. Everything else (full apportionment, Senate classes, RCV/STV/EC, governing/legislature, the causal-graph viz, MapLibre, Web Worker, multi-state data) is stubbed behind feature flags. The defining acceptance test is a single deterministic node test: createGame(seed) + the scripted action/tick log replays to a byte-identical serialize() across two runs and across a serialize->deserialize->continue, proving the engine contract before any breadth is added.
designTensions: RNG representation conflict: Core specifies a serializable RngState struct; Campaign (SeededRng) and Governing (Rng with fork()/nextFloat()) specify objects-with-methods. Resolution: the serializable RngState struct + pure functions (nextU32/forkRng) are canonical and live in GameState.rngStreams; a thin stateless Rng cursor wrapper provides the .fork()/.float() ergonomics the other two subsystems want but holds no hidden state and serializes back to RngState. All three now share one implementation.

Two effect-bridge types for one concept: Campaign emits ElectorateEffect, Governing emits EffectOp/ScheduledEffect. Both are 'a lagged, attributed delta to the sim'. Resolution: a single core ScheduledEffect with a discriminated EffectTarget. The 'electorate' target variant carries Campaign's segment reach + tone; simValue/groupHappiness/situation/economy variants carry Governing's policy deltas. One ledger, one ramp/decay/sunset math, one consumer contract for the electorate/economy.

Time model mismatch: Core uses dayIndex + tickCount; Campaign uses daysElapsed/electionDay as local day indices; Governing uses an opaque 'tick'. Resolution: Calendar.dayIndex is the single authoritative clock. Subsystems store ABSOLUTE DayIndex values (electionDay, resolveDay, enactedDay) not relative offsets, and 'tick' everywhere means calendar.tickCount. Governing's per-tick advanceLegislation is invoked by the core tickReducer's subsystemTicks step.

Ideology granularity: Electorate models per-issue positions Record<IssueId,number>; Governing and Campaign use a coarse 5-axis IdeologyVector. Resolution: per-issue positions are the fine-grained source of truth (voters, candidate platforms); IdeologyVector is a DERIVED projection (deriveIdeology(positions)) used only where a low-dimensional summary is needed (legislator cosine-distance utility, bill net position, map coloring). Never store both as independent truth.

RNG-purity boundary for evaluation: Electorate insists evaluateElectorate is RNG-free and only polling/opinion-ticks take rng; Governing wants whip-count actual votes to draw a seeded jitter; Campaign wants rngJitter in the effect magnitude. Resolution: keep the DETERMINISTIC core (utility/share/turnout, whip p_yea expectation, base effect magnitude) RNG-free so projections/previews are stable, and confine all draws to clearly-named forked sub-streams at the moment of resolution (actual vote draw, poll sample, effect jitter). Election-night AllocationResult is computed from the deterministic expected shares + one seeded sampling draw, so it is replayable.

State-ownership overlap: Electoral defines Candidacy.campaignId and Officeholder.personId; Campaign defines CandidateState.officeContestId; Governing defines Legislator/ExecutiveOffice holders; all reference 'a person'. Resolution: foreign-key-only discipline — each subsystem owns ONE slice of EntityStores and references others by EntityId string, never by nesting objects. A thin shared 'person/politician' identity (id, name, party, ideology) is the join key; rich personas live in whichever subsystem owns them, and core never inspects slice internals.

Validation/schema location: UI wants Zod schemas shared with the engine boundary, but the engine must stay DOM/IO-free and must not import @ui. Resolution: shared Zod schemas live in @data/schemas (neutral), imported by both the engine's validateAction and the UI's react-hook-form resolvers, with an ESLint no-restricted-imports boundary preventing @engine from importing @ui and presentational components/viz from importing @engine/@data.

Worker vs inline engine + selector memo churn: UI proposes a Web Worker EngineClient and revision-keyed memoization, but heavy structured-clone per tick and per-micro-mutation revision bumps could dominate. Resolution for phase 1: ship InlineEngineClient only (Worker behind ff.worker), and bump GameState.meta.revision exactly once per applyAction/tick (coarse) so selector caches keyed on revision stay valid for a whole tick. Worker + diff-shipping is a later optimization that does not change call sites because both implement the same EngineClient interface.
